blackbox.does: Counts distinct active entities over trailing daily, weekly, and monthly windows anchored on each date, using distinct entity counts so a single entity is never double counted within a window.

problem_solution.problem: Active-user counts require distinct entities over trailing windows anchored per date, and the windows nest so the daily count can never exceed the weekly which can never exceed the monthly.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sums per-day active counts to get a weekly total, double counting entities that were active on multiple days.
problem_solution.solution: A step that computes distinct active entities over each trailing window anchored on the date and preserves the nesting invariant.
common_inputs: activity events with entity id and date
common_outputs: result set with DAU, WAU, MAU per date
known_pitfalls: summing daily counts into a weekly total
success_signals: DAU is at most WAU is at most MAU on every date
counts use distinct entities, not event counts

blackbox.does: Flags timeseries points whose value deviates from a trailing rolling baseline by more than a configured number of robust deviations, using only past-window statistics to avoid lookahead.

problem_solution.problem: A threshold-based anomaly flag compares each point to a trailing baseline, and the baseline must exclude the current and future points so the flag is not contaminated by the value it is judging.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent computes the baseline over the whole series including the current point, so a large spike inflates its own baseline and is never flagged.
problem_solution.solution: A step that builds the baseline from a strictly trailing window, measures the robust deviation of the current point, and flags it above the threshold.
common_inputs: ordered timeseries with rolling baseline stats
common_outputs: result set with anomaly flag and deviation score
success_signals: the flag depends only on trailing statistics
the same series yields the same flags on rerun

blackbox.does: Credits each conversion entirely to the first marketing touch in the ordered path within the lookback window, emitting one full-credit attribution row per conversion.

problem_solution.problem: First-touch attribution assigns all conversion credit to the earliest qualifying touch, which requires a correct ordered path and a lookback window so pre-window touches are excluded.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent picks the first touch overall ignoring the lookback window, crediting a touch that occurred before the attribution horizon.
problem_solution.solution: A step that orders each conversion's touch path, filters to the lookback window, and assigns full credit to the earliest remaining touch.
common_inputs: touch events with channel and timestamp
common_outputs: result set with full credit to first touch
known_pitfalls: conversions with no in-window touch dropped silently
success_signals: credit per conversion sums to exactly one
the credited touch is the earliest in-window touch

blackbox.does: Credits each conversion entirely to the last marketing touch preceding it in the ordered path within the lookback window, emitting one full-credit attribution row per conversion.

problem_solution.problem: Last-touch attribution assigns all credit to the most recent qualifying touch before the conversion, which must exclude touches after the conversion and outside the lookback window.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent picks the maximum-timestamp touch without bounding it before the conversion, crediting a touch that happened after the sale.
problem_solution.solution: A step that orders the path, keeps touches strictly before the conversion within the lookback window, and credits the latest one fully.
common_inputs: touch events with channel and timestamp
common_outputs: result set with full credit to last touch
known_pitfalls: crediting a touch after the conversion
success_signals: credit per conversion sums to exactly one
the credited touch precedes the conversion

blackbox.does: Distributes each conversion's credit across all qualifying touches in the path using a configured weighting rule such as linear, position-based, or time-decay, so the fractions sum to one.

problem_solution.problem: Multi-touch attribution splits conversion credit across the touch path by a weighting rule, and the fractional credits for a conversion must sum to exactly one regardless of the rule.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies a time-decay weight but forgets to normalize, so the per-conversion credits do not sum to one and channel totals are inflated.
problem_solution.solution: A step that computes raw weights per touch under the chosen rule, normalizes them to sum to one per conversion, and emits one credited row per touch.
common_outputs: result set with fractional credit per touch
known_pitfalls: weights not normalized to sum to one
empty path leaving a conversion unattributed
success_signals: fractional credits sum to one per conversion
channel totals reconcile to total conversions

blackbox.does: Flags each entity as churned when the elapsed time since its last activity as of a reference date exceeds the inactivity threshold, emitting one deterministic flag per entity.

problem_solution.problem: A churn flag depends on a reference as-of date and an inactivity threshold, and the same inputs must always yield the same flag so downstream churn rates are stable.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses the current wall-clock time instead of a fixed as-of date, so re-running the same model on a different day flips flags nondeterministically.
problem_solution.solution: A step that measures the gap between each entity's last activity and an explicit as-of date, flagging churn when the gap exceeds the threshold.
common_inputs: activity events with entity id and date
common_outputs: result set with churn flag per entity
known_pitfalls: using wall-clock time instead of an as-of date
entities with no activity treated inconsistently
success_signals: the same as-of date yields identical flags on rerun
the flag matches the gap-versus-threshold comparison

title: Cohort Table Build

blackbox.does: Assigns each entity to a cohort by its first-activity period and pivots subsequent activity into a cohort-by-age-period grid keyed on cohort period and offset.

problem_solution.problem: Cohort analysis groups entities by the period they first appeared and then measures how each group behaves over its own age, but the cohort assignment must be a single stable first-touch period per entity.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent buckets rows by calendar period rather than by each entity's first period, so the same entity lands in multiple cohorts and the age axis is meaningless.
problem_solution.solution: A build step that computes one first-activity period per entity, derives the age offset for each later activity, and aggregates into a cohort x age-offset grid.
common_inputs: event rows with entity id and timestamp
common_outputs: cohort table keyed by cohort period and offset
known_pitfalls: bucketing by calendar period instead of first-touch
age offset computed from wrong anchor
success_signals: each entity appears in exactly one cohort
offset zero equals the cohort size

source_ref_families: product analytics cohort and retention definitions

blackbox.does: Computes the fraction of entities that reached a target event after a qualifying start event within a conversion window, reporting a bounded rate per cohort of starters.

problem_solution.problem: A conversion rate divides entities that reached a target event by those that started, and the target must be required to follow the start within a defined window to count.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent counts any target event regardless of order or window, so conversions that preceded the start inflate the rate above the real value.
problem_solution.solution: A step that anchors on qualifying starters, checks for a target event after the start within the window, and divides converters by starters.
common_outputs: result set with conversion rate per cohort
success_signals: the rate lies between zero and one
converters never exceed starters

blackbox.does: Computes aggregates for every combination of the listed dimensions, producing the full cross-tabulation of subtotals from the finest grain to the grand total.

problem_solution.problem: A cube materializes every subset of the dimension list, so the number of grouping sets grows as two to the power of the dimension count and must be bounded deliberately.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent cubes a high-cardinality dimension set without guardrails and produces an explosion of subtotal rows that overwhelms the output.
problem_solution.solution: A step that enumerates all dimension subsets, aggregates additive measures, tags each row with its active dimensions, and caps the dimension count against a limit.
success_signals: the grand-total row equals the ungrouped aggregate
each row identifies its active dimension subset

blackbox.does: Accumulates a measure from the start of each ordered partition to the current row using an unbounded-preceding to current-row frame, yielding a running cumulative total.

problem_solution.problem: A cumulative sum must add the measure from the partition start up to and including the current ordered row, which depends on a correctly bounded frame and a deterministic order.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves the default frame that extends to the current peer group under range mode, so ties collapse into the same cumulative value unexpectedly.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that sums with an explicit unbounded-preceding to current-row rows frame following the declared order.
success_signals: final cumulative value equals the partition total
cumulative sum is non-decreasing for non-negative measures

blackbox.does: Keeps exactly one row per business key by ranking duplicates on an ordering rule and retaining the latest, breaking ties deterministically so the output has a unique key.

problem_solution.problem: Deduplicating to the latest row per key requires a total ordering, because ties on the ordering column leave the survivor ambiguous and the output key non-unique.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent keeps the max-timestamp row but has multiple rows sharing that timestamp, so more than one row survives per key and the unique-key guarantee fails.
problem_solution.solution: A step that ranks rows per key by the ordering column plus a deterministic tiebreak and keeps only rank one, yielding one row per key.
common_outputs: deduplicated table with one row per key
known_pitfalls: dropping rows whose key is null
success_signals: the output key is unique
re-running the dedupe leaves the result unchanged

blackbox.does: Attaches the first and last ordered value of a target column across each partition to every row, using a full unbounded frame so last_value reflects the whole partition.

problem_solution.problem: Attaching each partition's first and last ordered value to every row requires the frame for last_value to span the whole partition, otherwise last_value returns the current row.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses last_value with the default current-row frame, so every row reports itself as the last value instead of the partition end.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that sets an unbounded-preceding to unbounded-following frame so first_value and last_value see the entire ordered partition.
common_outputs: windowed table with first and last value columns
known_pitfalls: default frame making last_value the current row
null target values skewing first and last
success_signals: last value equals the partition's final ordered value
input and output row counts match

blackbox.does: Counts the distinct entities that reached each ordered step of a conversion funnel, enforcing that a step is credited only when all prior steps occurred in sequence.

problem_solution.problem: A conversion funnel reports how many entities progressed through an ordered sequence of steps, and each step count must be a monotonically non-increasing subset of the step before it.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent counts each step independently, so a later step can show more entities than an earlier one and the funnel is internally inconsistent.
problem_solution.solution: A build step that requires the ordered prerequisite events per entity before crediting a step, yielding non-increasing counts down the funnel.
common_inputs: event rows with entity id, event name, timestamp
known_pitfalls: later step exceeding an earlier step
ignoring the time window between steps
success_signals: step counts never increase down the funnel
one row per funnel step in order

blackbox.does: Derives the step-to-step conversion and drop-off ratios from an ordered funnel table, reporting both the fraction that advanced and the fraction lost at each transition.

problem_solution.problem: Funnel optimization needs the conversion and drop-off rate at each transition, expressed as bounded fractions of the immediately preceding step.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent divides each step by the funnel entry count rather than the prior step, so the reported per-step drop-off does not reflect the local transition.
problem_solution.solution: A step that pairs each step with its predecessor, divides to get the advance rate, and reports drop-off as one minus that rate.
known_pitfalls: dividing by funnel entry instead of prior step
undefined transition when a step count is zero
success_signals: conversion plus drop-off equals one per transition
all rates fall between zero and one

title: Gap And Island

blackbox.does: Collapses an ordered sequence into contiguous islands of consecutive values and the gaps between them by grouping on the difference between the value and its dense position.

problem_solution.problem: The gaps-and-islands pattern identifies runs of consecutive values within a partition, which requires a stable island key derived from the offset between the value and its ordered position.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent detects breaks with a self-join on value plus one and misses runs when duplicates or the ordering step size vary, splitting islands incorrectly.
problem_solution.solution: A step that assigns a dense ordered position, computes the value-minus-position offset as an island key, and aggregates each island's bounds.
common_outputs: result set with island start, end, and length
success_signals: islands partition the input with no overlap
island row counts reconcile to the input rows

source_ref_families: gaps and islands SQL pattern literature

blackbox.does: Computes aggregates over several explicitly listed grouping sets in one pass and tags each output row with which dimensions were grouped versus rolled up.

problem_solution.problem: Grouping sets produce several aggregation grains in one query, and each output row must be unambiguously labeled with which dimensions were active so aggregated nulls are not confused with data nulls.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent unions separate group-by queries and cannot tell a rolled-up null from a genuine null dimension value in the combined result.
problem_solution.solution: A step that evaluates the listed grouping sets together and emits a grouping indicator per dimension to mark subtotal rows.
known_pitfalls: confusing subtotal nulls with data nulls
success_signals: every row identifies its active dimensions
subtotal rows are distinguishable from detail rows

blackbox.does: Assigns each measure value to a numeric bucket using equal-width or supplied bin edges and counts the rows per bucket, so the bucket counts sum back to the input row total.

problem_solution.problem: A histogram bins a measure into ranges and counts rows per bin, and the bin edges plus the treatment of out-of-range and boundary values must be explicit so every row lands in exactly one bin.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses inclusive edges on both sides so boundary values fall into two bins, and the bin counts no longer sum to the row total.
problem_solution.solution: A step that applies half-open bin intervals with an explicit out-of-range policy so each row maps to exactly one bucket and counts reconcile.
success_signals: bucket counts sum to the input row count
each row maps to exactly one bucket

blackbox.does: Attaches the prior and next row values within each ordered partition and computes the period-over-period delta and percent change against the lagged value.

problem_solution.problem: Period-over-period change requires each row to see the previous and next row within its ordered partition so a delta and percent change can be computed against the correct neighbor.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent self-joins on a hand-computed prior key that skips gaps, so the lag lands on the wrong period when periods are missing.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that reads the adjacent ordered value with lag and lead, handles the partition edge as null, and derives delta and percent change.
common_outputs: windowed table with prior, next, delta, percent change
known_pitfalls: division by zero on a zero prior value
edge rows not treated as null neighbors
success_signals: first and last rows have null neighbors
input and output row counts match

blackbox.does: Aggregates each customer's historical net contribution over their observed lifespan to a customer lifetime value, disclosing the observation window and excluding refunds.

problem_solution.problem: Lifetime value sums each customer's net contribution over an observed window, and the window plus the treatment of refunds and taxes must be explicit so the figure is a measured historical value rather than an unbounded projection.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sums gross revenue including refunds and taxes and presents it as lifetime value without stating the observation window, overstating the number.
problem_solution.solution: A step that nets refunds and taxes, sums contribution per customer within a disclosed observation window, and labels the value as historical-to-date.
common_outputs: result set with historical lifetime value per customer
known_pitfalls: including refunds or taxes in contribution
presenting historical value as a forward projection
success_signals: value nets refunds and taxes as configured
the observation window is stated on every row

blackbox.does: Mines item co-occurrence within baskets to produce item-pair association rules with support, confidence, and lift, filtered by minimum-support and confidence thresholds.

problem_solution.problem: Market-basket analysis derives association rules from item co-occurrence, and support, confidence, and lift must follow their exact definitions with a minimum-support floor to avoid a combinatorial pair explosion.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent counts co-occurrence but computes confidence with the wrong denominator or omits the support floor, surfacing spurious rules from rare pairs.
problem_solution.solution: A step that counts single-item and pair baskets, applies the minimum-support prune, and computes confidence and lift from the correct marginals.
common_outputs: result set of association rules with support, confidence, lift
known_pitfalls: no minimum-support floor causing pair explosion
success_signals: support and confidence lie between zero and one
lift above one marks positive association

blackbox.does: Computes the median together with the first and third quartiles and the interquartile range per group as a robust summary of central tendency and spread.

problem_solution.problem: A robust summary reports the median with the first and third quartiles and their difference, and all three quantiles must use the same definition so the ordering q1 <= median <= q3 always holds.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reports the mean as a stand-in for the median or mixes quartile methods, so the spread is misleading and ordering can invert.
problem_solution.solution: A step that computes q1, median, and q3 with one consistent percentile method and derives the interquartile range as q3 minus q1.
common_outputs: result set with median, q1, q3, and IQR per group
known_pitfalls: substituting the mean for the median
success_signals: q1 is at most median is at most q3 per group
IQR equals q3 minus q1

blackbox.does: Compares each month's metric to the immediately preceding month on an aligned monthly spine and reports the month-over-month absolute and percent change.

problem_solution.problem: Month-over-month growth compares consecutive months, which requires a dense monthly spine so a month with no activity still participates as a zero rather than being skipped.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent lags over present months only, so a silent month gap makes a later month appear to follow the wrong predecessor.
problem_solution.solution: A step that densifies to a monthly spine, offsets by one month, and computes month-over-month delta and percent change.
common_outputs: result set with current, prior-month, growth
known_pitfalls: mixing partial current month with full prior months
division by a zero prior month
success_signals: consecutive months are always aligned
empty months appear as zero, not skipped

blackbox.does: Computes a rolling z-score for each point as its deviation from the trailing-window mean divided by the trailing-window standard deviation, guarding against a zero-variance window.

problem_solution.problem: A moving z-score standardizes each point against a trailing window, so the mean and standard deviation must come from the same past frame and a zero-variance frame must be handled without dividing by zero.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent divides by a window standard deviation that is zero on a flat stretch, producing infinities or nulls that break downstream flags.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that computes the trailing mean and standard deviation over the same frame and returns a defined value or null when variance is zero.
known_pitfalls: mismatched frames for mean and stddev
success_signals: zero-variance windows yield a defined result, not an error
input and output row counts match

blackbox.does: Classifies each period's active entities as new or returning by comparing their first-seen period to the current period, so new plus returning reconciles to the active total.

problem_solution.problem: Splitting active entities into new and returning depends on a correct first-seen period per entity, and the two classes must partition the active set without overlap or omission.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent recomputes first-seen from the filtered current window, so entities look new every period and the returning count collapses.
problem_solution.solution: A step that resolves each entity's global first-seen period once, then labels a current-period entity new when the two match and returning otherwise.
common_inputs: activity events with entity id and period
common_outputs: result set with new and returning counts per period
known_pitfalls: recomputing first-seen from a filtered window
success_signals: new plus returning equals the active total
each entity is new in exactly one period

title: Pareto ABC Classification

blackbox.does: Ranks items by contribution, accumulates their share of the total, and assigns A, B, or C classes at the configured cumulative-share cutoffs following the Pareto principle.

problem_solution.problem: ABC classification orders items by contribution and cuts them into classes at cumulative-share thresholds, which requires the cumulative share to be computed over a correctly ordered and normalized total.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent computes each item's individual share and thresholds on that instead of the running cumulative share, so the class boundaries are wrong.
problem_solution.solution: A step that sorts by descending contribution, accumulates the normalized share, and assigns classes at the configured cumulative cutoffs.
common_outputs: result set with cumulative share and ABC class
known_pitfalls: thresholding individual instead of cumulative share
cumulative share not normalized to one
success_signals: cumulative share rises monotonically to one
one class assignment per item

source_ref_families: Pareto and ABC inventory analysis literature

blackbox.does: Computes the relative standing of each row within its partition as a percent rank and a cumulative distribution, both bounded in the zero-to-one range by definition.

problem_solution.problem: Relative standing expresses where a row sits within its partition on a normalized scale, and percent rank and cumulative distribution have distinct definitions that must not be conflated.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent computes rank divided by row count and calls it percent rank, missing the minus-one adjustment and producing values that never reach zero.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that emits percent_rank as (rank minus one) over (rows minus one) and cume_dist as the fraction of rows at or below the current value.
common_outputs: windowed table with percent rank and cume dist
known_pitfalls: values falling outside zero to one
success_signals: all values lie between zero and one
the top ordered row has cume dist equal to one

blackbox.does: Computes requested percentiles of a measure per group using either the continuous or discrete percentile definition as configured, so the interpolation method is explicit.

problem_solution.problem: Percentiles depend on the definition chosen, since continuous interpolation and discrete selection give different values, so the method must be declared and applied consistently.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent mixes an approximate percentile function with an exact one across groups, so percentiles are not comparable and monotonicity breaks.
problem_solution.solution: A step that applies a single declared percentile definition per requested quantile and per group, keeping the interpolation method uniform.
common_outputs: result set with percentile values per group
success_signals: percentiles increase with the quantile level
the declared method is recorded on output

blackbox.does: Aligns each period's metric with the corresponding prior period on a calendar spine and reports the absolute and relative change against a comparison offset.

problem_solution.problem: Comparing a metric to a prior period requires aligning on a complete calendar spine so missing periods are treated as zero or null rather than silently skipped.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent lags over the present rows only, so a gap in the data shifts the comparison onto the wrong prior period.
problem_solution.solution: A step that joins the metric onto a dense period spine, offsets by the requested comparison distance, and computes absolute and percent change.
common_outputs: result set with current, prior, delta, percent change
known_pitfalls: skipping missing periods instead of zero-filling
division by a zero prior value
success_signals: every period has an aligned prior comparison
gaps surface as explicit zero or null, not skips

blackbox.does: Accumulates a metric from the start of the enclosing period to each row, producing month-to-date, quarter-to-date, and year-to-date running totals that reset at each period boundary.

problem_solution.problem: Period-to-date totals accumulate within a calendar period and must reset exactly at each period boundary, so the partitioning key has to match the enclosing period.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent accumulates across the whole series without partitioning by the enclosing period, so the to-date total never resets and grows unbounded.
problem_solution.solution: A step that partitions the running sum by the enclosing period and accumulates in date order so each period restarts at zero.
common_outputs: result set with to-date running total
known_pitfalls: failing to reset at the period boundary
success_signals: to-date total resets at each period start
the period-end to-date equals the period total

blackbox.does: Rotates a long key-value table into a wide table by turning distinct category values into columns and aggregating the measure per row-key and category cell.

problem_solution.problem: Pivoting a long table to wide turns distinct category values into columns, which requires an explicit or discovered column set and an aggregation for cells that would otherwise collide.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hardcodes a category list and silently drops rows whose category is not in the list, losing measure totals.
problem_solution.solution: A step that enumerates the category domain, aggregates the measure per row-key and category, and materializes one column per category with a documented default for empty cells.
known_pitfalls: empty cells left null versus zero inconsistently
success_signals: unpivoting the result reproduces the input totals
one column exists per observed category

title: Retention Curve

blackbox.does: Divides each cohort's active count at every age offset by that cohort's size to produce a normalized retention ratio curve per cohort and an overall average curve.

problem_solution.problem: A retention curve normalizes each cohort's later activity against its own starting size so cohorts of different sizes can be compared on a common zero-to-one scale.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent divides by the wrong denominator, using the total base or the current-period count instead of the cohort's own size, so ratios exceed one and are not comparable.
problem_solution.solution: A ratio step that pins the denominator to each cohort's offset-zero size and emits a bounded retention value at every age offset.
known_pitfalls: ratios exceeding one from denominator errors
treating missing offsets as zero retention
success_signals: every retention value falls between zero and one
offset zero equals one for every cohort

source_ref_families: product analytics cohort and retention definitions

blackbox.does: Scores each customer on recency, frequency, and monetary value by quantile-binning each dimension into ordinal scores and combining them into an RFM segment label.

problem_solution.problem: RFM scoring bins recency, frequency, and monetary value into ordinal scores per customer, and the bin edges must come from the population distribution so scores are relative, not absolute cutoffs.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies hardcoded thresholds that do not fit the actual distribution, so nearly all customers fall into one bin and the segments carry no signal.
problem_solution.solution: A step that computes quantile bins per dimension, assigns ordinal scores, and concatenates them into a segment key with one row per customer.
common_outputs: result set with R, F, M scores and segment label
known_pitfalls: recency sign inverted so recent scores low
duplicate customer rows breaking the key
success_signals: each score falls within the configured band range
exactly one segmented row per customer

blackbox.does: Computes a trailing moving average of a measure over a fixed row or time frame within each ordered partition, honoring the frame bounds set by the window spec.

problem_solution.problem: A moving average smooths a measure over a trailing frame, and the frame must be defined precisely in rows or time so partial early frames are handled consistently.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent averages the whole partition or uses an unbounded frame, so early rows and the frame width are wrong and the smoothing is misleading.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that averages the measure over the exact trailing frame declared in the window spec, with a documented policy for partial leading frames.
known_pitfalls: unbounded frame instead of a trailing window
inconsistent handling of partial leading frames
mixing row frames with time frames
success_signals: moving average uses exactly the declared frame
input and output row counts match

blackbox.does: Produces a hierarchical rollup that aggregates along an ordered dimension list from the finest grain up to the grand total, emitting one subtotal level per prefix.

problem_solution.problem: A rollup aggregates along an ordered hierarchy so each subtotal level equals the sum of the detail rows beneath it, which only holds for additive measures.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent rolls up a non-additive measure such as a distinct count or an average, so the subtotals do not equal the sum of their children.
problem_solution.solution: A step that evaluates the hierarchical prefixes of the dimension list, aggregating additive measures and flagging non-additive ones for re-aggregation.
common_outputs: result set with hierarchical subtotals and grand total
known_pitfalls: wrong dimension order in the hierarchy
subtotal rows not distinguishable from details
success_signals: each subtotal equals the sum of its children
the top level equals the grand total

blackbox.does: Maintains a per-partition running balance by adding signed transaction amounts in order, producing the balance after each transaction and the closing balance per partition.

problem_solution.problem: A running balance adds signed amounts in strict order per account so each row shows the balance immediately after that transaction, which requires a stable order across same-timestamp rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent orders only by date and lets same-day transactions reorder, so the running balance after each row is not reproducible.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that accumulates signed amounts over an unbounded-preceding to current-row frame with a deterministic sequence tiebreak.
success_signals: closing balance equals the signed sum per account
re-running yields the identical balance sequence

blackbox.does: Splits a regular timeseries into trend, seasonal, and residual components at a declared period using moving-average trend and periodic seasonal averaging under an additive model.

problem_solution.problem: Seasonal decomposition separates a series into trend, seasonal, and residual parts, which requires a regular time grid and a declared season length so the components reconstruct the observed value.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent decomposes an irregular series with gaps or guesses the period, so the seasonal component absorbs trend and the parts do not sum back to the observation.
problem_solution.solution: A step that regularizes the grid, estimates trend by a centered moving average, averages detrended values per season index, and takes the residual so components reconstruct the input.
common_outputs: result set with trend, seasonal, residual
known_pitfalls: components not summing to the observation
success_signals: trend plus seasonal plus residual equals the observed value
the seasonal component repeats with the declared period

blackbox.does: Groups an ordered event stream per entity into sessions by starting a new session whenever the inactivity gap to the prior event exceeds the configured timeout.

problem_solution.problem: Sessionization partitions each entity's ordered events into sessions separated by inactivity gaps, and every event must map to exactly one session with a stable session identifier.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent groups by calendar day or a fixed window instead of the inactivity gap, splitting active sessions and merging distinct ones.
problem_solution.solution: An ordered scan per entity that opens a new session when the timestamp gap from the previous event exceeds the timeout and assigns an incrementing session key.
common_inputs: event rows with entity id and timestamp
common_outputs: session table with session id per event
known_pitfalls: using a fixed window instead of the gap
success_signals: every event belongs to exactly one session
re-running yields identical session boundaries

blackbox.does: Captures a periodic snapshot of a slowly changing metric per entity, emitting one row per entity per snapshot period with the metric value effective as of that period boundary.

problem_solution.problem: A slowly changing metric is snapshotted per period so its history is queryable, and each snapshot must reflect the value effective as of the period boundary with one row per entity per period.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent snapshots the current value for all past periods, overwriting history so every period shows today's figure instead of the point-in-time value.
problem_solution.solution: A step that resolves the metric value effective at each period boundary and writes one immutable snapshot row per entity per period.
common_outputs: result set with per-period metric snapshots
known_pitfalls: overwriting history with the current value
duplicate snapshots for the same entity-period
boundary value taken from the wrong side
success_signals: one snapshot row per entity per period
re-running a period reproduces the same snapshot

blackbox.does: Divides the daily active count by the monthly active count on each date to produce the DAU-over-MAU stickiness ratio, a bounded engagement measure between zero and one.

problem_solution.problem: Stickiness divides the daily active count by the monthly active count on the same date, so both inputs must use consistent distinct-entity definitions and the same anchor date.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent divides a daily count by a lagged or misaligned monthly count, producing a ratio that can exceed one and mislead on engagement.
problem_solution.solution: A step that joins DAU and MAU on the anchor date and divides, guarding the monthly denominator against zero.
common_inputs: active-user result set with DAU and MAU
common_outputs: result set with stickiness ratio per date
known_pitfalls: ratio exceeding one from inconsistent definitions
success_signals: stickiness lies between zero and one
DAU and MAU share the same anchor date

blackbox.does: Selects the highest-ranked N rows within each partition by the ordering keys, resolving ties by a deterministic tiebreak so exactly N rows are kept per group.

problem_solution.problem: Top-N per group returns only the leading N rows within each partition, and ties at the boundary must resolve deterministically so the result is reproducible.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies a global limit or filters after a non-deterministic rank, so different groups return different counts or the boundary flips between runs.
problem_solution.solution: A step that assigns a deterministic per-partition row number and keeps positions one through N, guaranteeing at most N rows per group.
common_outputs: result set with the top N rows per group
known_pitfalls: returning more than N on ties with rank
success_signals: each group returns at most N rows
the same rows are kept on every rerun

blackbox.does: Melts a set of measure columns from a wide table into category and value pairs, emitting one long row per non-null measure cell while preserving the identifier columns.

problem_solution.problem: Unpivoting melts a declared set of measure columns into category-value pairs, and the policy for null cells must be explicit so the row count is predictable and the inverse of a pivot.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent unions the columns but keeps null cells inconsistently, so the long row count does not match the non-null cell count and a later pivot cannot round-trip.
problem_solution.solution: A step that reads the column list from the schema spec, emits one long row per selected cell with a documented null policy, and carries the identifier columns through.
known_pitfalls: mixed data types across melted columns
success_signals: re-pivoting the long output restores the wide table
long row count matches the selected non-null cells

blackbox.does: Ranks rows within each partition by the ordering keys with tied rows sharing a rank and no gaps, so ranks form a contiguous sequence of distinct values.

problem_solution.problem: Dense rank must number distinct ordered values contiguously so that ties share a rank and the next distinct value is exactly one higher, with no skipped ranks.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses rank and leaves gaps after ties, so the maximum dense rank no longer equals the number of distinct values.
problem_solution.solution: A window step applying dense-rank semantics: each new distinct order-key value increments the rank by one regardless of tie-group size.
common_outputs: windowed table with dense rank column
known_pitfalls: treating nulls as a distinct extra value unexpectedly
success_signals: ranks are contiguous with no gaps
max dense rank equals distinct value count

blackbox.does: Splits each ordered partition into the requested number of as-evenly-sized buckets and labels every row with its one-based bucket ordinal.

problem_solution.problem: Ntile bucketing partitions ordered rows into a fixed number of near-equal groups, and when the row count is not divisible the extra rows must land in the earliest buckets by definition.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent bucketizes by value range instead of by rank position, producing wildly uneven bucket sizes that misrepresent quartiles.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that ntiles by ordered position so bucket sizes differ by at most one row and the remainder fills the lowest ordinals.
known_pitfalls: bucketing by value range not rank position
remainder rows placed in the wrong buckets
bucket count exceeding partition row count
success_signals: bucket sizes differ by at most one row
bucket ordinals span one through the requested count

blackbox.does: Ranks rows within each partition by the ordering keys, assigning tied rows the same rank and leaving gaps after ties as standard rank semantics require.

problem_solution.problem: Rank must give tied rows the same rank and then skip ranks so the next distinct value reflects how many rows preceded it, unlike dense rank or row number.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses row_number and hides ties, or uses dense_rank and removes the gaps, so the rank no longer reflects standing among all rows.
problem_solution.solution: A window step applying rank semantics: equal order keys share a rank and the following rank jumps by the count of tied rows.
known_pitfalls: unstable ranks from an ambiguous order
success_signals: tied rows share the same rank
rank gaps equal the size of each tie group

blackbox.does: Assigns a gapless sequential position to each row within its partition following the ordering of the window spec, breaking ties deterministically by a tiebreak key.

problem_solution.problem: Row numbering must give each row a unique position within its partition following a defined order, which requires a deterministic tiebreak so the numbering is reproducible.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent orders only by a column with ties and no tiebreak, so which row gets which number changes between runs and downstream picks are unstable.
problem_solution.solution: A window step that partitions, orders by the requested keys plus a deterministic tiebreak, and emits a one-based sequential position.
common_outputs: windowed table with row number column
known_pitfalls: confusing row_number with rank on ties
success_signals: row numbers are unique within each partition
input and output row counts match

blackbox.does: Compares each week's metric to the prior week on an aligned weekly spine using a consistent week-start convention and reports the week-over-week change.

problem_solution.problem: Week-over-week growth depends on a single consistent week-start convention, because mixing week definitions shifts the boundary and corrupts the comparison.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent truncates to week with a default that disagrees with the rest of the model, so weeks are offset by a day and totals double count or miss days.
problem_solution.solution: A step that pins the week-start convention, densifies to a weekly spine, offsets by one week, and computes the change.
common_outputs: result set with current, prior-week, growth
known_pitfalls: partial trailing week compared to full weeks
success_signals: all weeks use the same start convention
consecutive weeks are always aligned

blackbox.does: Compares each period's metric to the same period one year earlier on an aligned calendar spine and reports the year-over-year absolute and percent change.

problem_solution.problem: Year-over-year growth aligns each period with the same period one year prior, which must respect the calendar so leap years and month lengths map to the correct anchor.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent subtracts a fixed number of rows instead of a calendar year, so weekly or daily grains land on the wrong prior anchor.
problem_solution.solution: A step that offsets by one calendar year on the period spine and computes the year-over-year delta and percent change.
common_outputs: result set with current, prior-year, growth
known_pitfalls: fixed row offset instead of a calendar year
zero prior-year value breaking percent change
success_signals: each period aligns to the correct prior-year anchor
growth is null where no prior-year value exists

blackbox.does: Builds and updates an accumulating snapshot fact with one row per process instance, filling milestone date and lag columns in place as the instance advances, and returns a merge receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Pipeline processes with defined milestones (order to ship to deliver) need one evolving row per instance that records each milestone date and the lag between them.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent appends a new row at every milestone, so one order becomes many rows and lag calculations require self-joins that miscount.
problem_solution.solution: An accumulating snapshot with one row per process instance, keyed on the instance, whose milestone date and lag columns are merged in place as later events arrive.
known_pitfalls: duplicate instance rows from appending instead of merging
non-idempotent re-runs re-filling milestone columns wrongly
lag columns going negative on out-of-order events
success_signals: one row per process instance
re-running the same events changes no milestone values

blackbox.does: Builds a bridge table resolving a many-to-many relationship between two dimensions into one row per valid pair, optionally with allocation weights, and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Many-to-many relationships between dimensions (accounts to customers, products to categories) cannot live on a single fact without double counting.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins the two dimensions directly in the fact, so measures are counted once per pair and totals explode.
problem_solution.solution: A bridge table with one row per valid dimension pair, keyed on both surrogates, that optionally carries allocation weights so measures can be apportioned rather than duplicated.
known_pitfalls: allocation weights that do not sum to one per group
orphan pairs referencing a missing dimension row
success_signals: each dimension pair appears once
weights sum to one within each bridged group

blackbox.does: Clones a source relation into a target using the warehouse zero-copy clone so the target holds the same rows as the source at clone time, and returns a materialization receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Standing up a cheap environment copy or a defer target needs a relation with identical contents to production without paying a full copy cost.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent recreates the environment with create-table-as-select, so it pays full storage and compute and the copy diverges from the source it should mirror.
problem_solution.solution: A zero-copy clone that points a target relation at the source's underlying storage, giving identical contents at clone time that later diverge only when written.
known_pitfalls: cloning to a target that already holds needed data
assuming the clone tracks later source changes
success_signals: the clone holds the same rows as the source at clone time
re-cloning to the same target yields identical contents

blackbox.does: Builds a conformed dimension by aligning attribute names, domains, and surrogate keys across marts under a conformance policy so facts share one dimension definition.

problem_solution.problem: When each mart defines its own copy of a shared dimension, the same customer or date has different keys and attribute names, so cross-mart analysis breaks.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent rebuilds a per-mart date dimension with different surrogate keys, so a drill-across between two facts cannot align on the shared dimension.
problem_solution.solution: A single conformed dimension with agreed attribute names, domains, and surrogate keys that every mart references, enabling drill-across on the shared grain.
known_pitfalls: surrogate keys that differ across marts
attribute domains that disagree between sources
silent divergence when one mart forks the dimension
success_signals: all marts join on the same surrogate key
attribute domains match the conformance contract

blackbox.does: Resolves a model's target database, schema, and relation alias from custom naming macros and config so the built relation lands in the intended physical location, and records the resolution.

problem_solution.problem: Teams need control over where models physically land - custom target schemas per layer and stable aliases - without the default schema-concatenation surprising them.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent relies on the default schema behavior that prefixes the target schema, so models land in an unexpected schema and consumers cannot find them.
problem_solution.solution: A resolver that applies the project's custom schema and alias macros to compute the final database, schema, and relation name for each model deterministically.
known_pitfalls: default schema concatenation landing models unexpectedly
two models resolving to the same relation and colliding
success_signals: each model lands in its intended schema
no two models resolve to the same physical relation

blackbox.does: Builds a dimension table with one row per business entity, a surrogate key, descriptive attributes, and an unknown-member row, and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Facts need conformed descriptive context keyed by a stable surrogate, and dimensions must stay unique per entity with a defined member for unmatched facts.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent keys the dimension on the natural id only and omits an unknown member, so facts with missing or late-arriving keys drop out of joins.
problem_solution.solution: A dimension with a deterministic surrogate key, one row per entity, and a reserved unknown/-1 member so every fact row can always join.
known_pitfalls: duplicate surrogate keys from a non-unique natural key
no unknown member so unmatched facts vanish
attributes at a finer grain than the declared entity
success_signals: surrogate key is unique and not null
every fact foreign key resolves to a dimension row

blackbox.does: Attaches model and column descriptions from documentation blocks to the model metadata and assembles them into the generated documentation catalog, returning a contract report.

problem_solution.problem: Consumers cannot tell what a model or column means without documentation, and descriptions duplicated across models drift out of sync.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves columns undocumented or pastes the same description into many models, so meanings are unclear and updates miss some copies.
problem_solution.solution: A docs attach that binds reusable documentation blocks to models and columns and compiles them into the catalog, so descriptions are defined once and surfaced consistently.
known_pitfalls: descriptions drifting from the actual columns
success_signals: models and columns carry descriptions in the catalog
shared descriptions come from one reusable block

blackbox.does: Registers an exposure that declares a downstream consumer of dbt models (a dashboard, application, or report) with its owner and upstream refs, extending lineage to the consumer.

problem_solution.problem: Lineage stops at the last dbt model, so no one can see which dashboards or applications depend on a model before changing or deprecating it.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent changes a mart with no record of its consumers, so a downstream dashboard breaks and the owner is discovered only after it fails.
problem_solution.solution: An exposure declaration that names the downstream consumer, its owner, and the models it depends on, extending the lineage graph so impact is visible before changes.
known_pitfalls: exposures that drift from the real consumers
success_signals: lineage shows which consumers depend on a model
changing a model surfaces its downstream exposures

blackbox.does: Builds a fact table at a declared event grain, replacing natural keys with dimension surrogate keys and carrying additive measures, and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: A fact table must record measurements at one event grain and reference dimensions by surrogate key so slices and aggregates stay correct.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves natural business keys on the fact and mixes two grains in one table, so joins fan out and sums over-count.
problem_solution.solution: A fact keyed to a single event grain that swaps natural keys for dimension surrogates via a key map and keeps only additive measures plus degenerate dimensions.
known_pitfalls: orphan facts whose surrogate lookup missed
non-additive measures summed as if additive
mixing header and line grains in one fact
success_signals: every foreign key matches a dimension surrogate
one row per declared event grain

blackbox.does: Drops an existing incremental relation and rebuilds it from scratch over the full source history, ignoring the incremental filter, and returns a materialization receipt.

problem_solution.problem: After a logic change or a corrupted incremental state, an incremental model must be rebuilt from the full source so its contents reflect the current transformation.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent edits incremental logic but keeps loading incrementally, so the historical rows retain the old logic and the table is internally inconsistent.
problem_solution.solution: A full-refresh rebuild that drops the relation and reconstructs it from the entire source under the current logic, restoring a consistent table that later incremental runs extend.
known_pitfalls: dropping a large table during business hours
a source that no longer holds the full history to rebuild from
downstream consumers reading during the rebuild window
success_signals: the rebuilt table reflects the current logic throughout
a second rebuild produces identical contents

blackbox.does: Runs the generic accepted-values test asserting a column contains only values from a declared allowed set, and returns a test receipt with any unexpected values.

problem_solution.problem: Status and category columns are expected to hold a small fixed set of values, but upstream systems occasionally introduce a new code that breaks case logic.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes case expressions over an assumed set of statuses, so a new upstream status falls through to a default bucket and skews reporting.
problem_solution.solution: A generic accepted-values test that fails when the column contains any value outside the declared allowed set, surfacing new codes before logic misbehaves.
known_pitfalls: case or whitespace differences flagged as unexpected
an allowed set that drifts from the real domain
success_signals: a new upstream code trips the test
the column holds only declared values

blackbox.does: Runs the generic not-null test on a declared column, passing only when no row holds a null in that column, and returns a test receipt with the count of nulls found.

problem_solution.problem: Columns that downstream logic treats as always present (keys, amounts, dates) break joins and math when a source starts emitting nulls.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent assumes a required column is never null, so an incoming null flows into a join key or a sum and produces missing rows or wrong totals.
problem_solution.solution: A generic not-null test on the required column that fails the run the moment a null appears, catching upstream data problems before they propagate.
known_pitfalls: testing a column that is legitimately nullable
empty strings that are not null but are still invalid
success_signals: a newly introduced null fails the test
the required column is confirmed fully populated

blackbox.does: Runs the generic relationships test asserting every value in a foreign-key column exists in the referenced parent column, and returns a test receipt with any orphan values.

problem_solution.problem: Facts reference dimensions by key, and the warehouse rarely enforces foreign keys, so orphan references accumulate and joins silently drop rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent trusts that every fact key matches a dimension row, so late-arriving or mistyped keys become orphans that vanish from inner joins.
problem_solution.solution: A generic relationships test that checks each child key value exists in the parent column and fails when orphan references are present.
known_pitfalls: ignoring nulls that should or should not count as orphans
pointing the test at the wrong parent grain
success_signals: an orphan foreign key trips the test
every child key resolves to a parent row

blackbox.does: Runs the generic uniqueness test on a declared column or expression, passing only when no value repeats, and returns a test receipt with any duplicate values found.

problem_solution.problem: Primary and surrogate keys must stay unique, but joins and merges can quietly introduce duplicates that inflate every downstream aggregate.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent assumes a column is unique and joins on it without asserting uniqueness, so a duplicate fans out rows and no one notices until totals are wrong.
problem_solution.solution: A generic uniqueness test declared on the key column or a composite expression that fails the run when any value appears more than once.
known_pitfalls: testing a single column when the real key is composite
null values slipping past a naive uniqueness check
success_signals: a duplicate key trips the test
the declared key proves unique across the table

blackbox.does: Applies the declared privilege grants on a model's relation after it is built, reconciling current grants to the desired set so consumers have the intended access, and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Rebuilding a relation can reset its privileges, so consumers lose access unless the intended grants are reapplied as part of the build.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent grants access manually once, so the next full rebuild drops the grants and downstream readers get permission errors.
problem_solution.solution: A grant step that declares the desired privileges and reconciles the relation's grants to that set after each build, restoring access idempotently.
known_pitfalls: grants dropped by a rebuild and never reapplied
success_signals: consumers keep access across rebuilds
re-applying the same grants changes nothing

blackbox.does: Runs an incremental model in append mode, selecting only new source rows past the last high-water mark and inserting them into the target, and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Immutable event streams are expensive to fully rebuild every run, and only rows newer than the last load actually need to be processed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent appends the whole source every run or picks a high-water mark with a boundary error, so it either reprocesses everything or double-inserts the edge rows.
problem_solution.solution: An append-mode incremental that filters the source to rows strictly past the recorded high-water mark and inserts them, with the boundary chosen so re-runs add no duplicates.
known_pitfalls: off-by-one boundary re-inserting the last batch
append mode used where late-updating rows need a merge
success_signals: re-running the same window appends no duplicate rows
only rows past the high-water mark are inserted

blackbox.does: Runs an incremental model in delete-insert mode, deleting target rows whose keys are in the new batch and inserting the batch, and returns a merge receipt with deleted and inserted counts.

problem_solution.problem: On engines without an efficient merge, updating an incremental target is best done by deleting the affected keys and reinserting the recomputed rows in one transaction.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deletes by key and inserts in separate uncommitted steps, so a failure between them leaves the target missing the deleted rows.
problem_solution.solution: A delete-insert incremental that, in one transaction, deletes rows whose keys appear in the batch and inserts the recomputed batch, keeping the target consistent on retry.
known_pitfalls: delete and insert split across transactions losing rows on failure
a key set that deletes more than the batch replaces
non-idempotent re-runs on the same batch
success_signals: re-running the batch leaves the target unchanged
each affected key ends with exactly the batch's rows

blackbox.does: Runs an incremental model in insert-overwrite mode, replacing whole target partitions selected by the run with freshly computed rows, and returns a run receipt listing overwritten partitions.

problem_solution.problem: On partitioned warehouses, reprocessing a day or region is cleanest by atomically replacing the affected partitions rather than merging row by row.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites without a bounded partition predicate, so a mistargeted run replaces the entire table instead of the intended partitions.
problem_solution.solution: An insert-overwrite incremental that computes rows only for the selected partitions and atomically swaps those partitions, leaving all others untouched.
known_pitfalls: an unbounded predicate overwriting the whole table
partition column mismatch overwriting the wrong slices
a static predicate missing newly appearing partitions
success_signals: only the selected partitions change
re-running the same partitions yields identical contents

blackbox.does: Runs an incremental model in merge mode, matching new rows to the target on a unique key to update changed rows and insert new keys, and returns a merge receipt with per-outcome counts.

problem_solution.problem: Incremental targets whose rows can change after first load must update the existing row for a key and insert genuinely new keys without creating duplicates.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent appends changed rows or defines a non-unique merge key, so a key ends up with several rows and the latest state is ambiguous.
problem_solution.solution: A merge-mode incremental keyed on a unique column that matches incoming rows to the target, updating on match and inserting on no-match so each key stays single-rowed.
known_pitfalls: a non-unique merge key duplicating rows
success_signals: re-applying the same batch changes nothing
each merge key resolves to exactly one row

blackbox.does: Applies an incremental predicate that narrows the target scan and the source window to the recent range being processed so an incremental run touches only relevant partitions.

problem_solution.problem: An incremental merge that scans the entire target to match a small recent batch does far more work than needed on large partitioned tables.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves the merge unbounded, so the engine scans the whole target every run even though only the last few partitions can match.
problem_solution.solution: An incremental predicate that restricts both the target match scan and the source read to the recent key or date window, so the run considers only the partitions that can change.
known_pitfalls: a predicate window narrower than the late-arriving data range
bounds not aligned to the partition column
success_signals: only recent partitions participate in the run
results match an equivalent unpruned run

blackbox.does: Builds an intermediate model that composes one or more staging tables into a reusable transformation step (join, unnest, or business-logic block) and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: A single mart query often bundles several distinct transformation steps, making it long, hard to test, and impossible to reuse across marts.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inlines every join and business rule into one giant mart model, so the same logic is copy-pasted into the next mart and drifts out of sync.
problem_solution.solution: An intermediate layer that isolates one purposeful transformation step, is materialized ephemerally or as a table, and is referenced by name from the marts that need it.
known_pitfalls: intermediate models that fan out into a deep dependency chain
reusing an intermediate for two grains it was not built for
success_signals: two marts reference the same intermediate instead of duplicating logic
each intermediate has a single clear responsibility

blackbox.does: Emits the resolved model dependency graph as a lineage artifact, listing each model's upstream sources and refs and downstream dependents, and returns a lineage receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Impact analysis and debugging need a machine-readable graph of which models feed which, derived from actual refs rather than tribal knowledge.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reasons about dependencies from memory, so it misses a hidden consumer and a change breaks a model it did not know existed.
problem_solution.solution: A lineage emit that resolves refs and sources across the project into an explicit dependency graph artifact consumers and tools can query for impact.
known_pitfalls: lineage missing edges from hard-coded relations
a stale graph emitted from an outdated manifest
success_signals: every ref appears as an edge in the graph
impact analysis matches the emitted lineage

blackbox.does: Expands a parametrized reusable SQL macro into a model's compiled SQL, applying the standardized transform (such as cents-to-dollars or a rename block) and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: The same SQL pattern (currency conversion, safe casts, a standard set of audit columns) recurs across many models and drifts when copy-pasted.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent copies the SQL snippet into each model, so a fix to the pattern must be applied by hand everywhere and some copies are missed.
problem_solution.solution: A macro that captures the pattern once as parametrized SQL and is invoked from each model, so a change to the macro updates every call site on the next build.
known_pitfalls: a macro with hidden environment assumptions
over-abstracting so the generated SQL is hard to debug
success_signals: fixing the macro updates every call site
call sites share one definition of the pattern

blackbox.does: Builds a business-facing mart model at a declared grain from intermediate tables, applying final naming and aggregation, and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Consumers need a stable, well-named, single-grain table for a business entity, not a pile of intermediate steps at mixed grains.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent ships a mart whose grain is ambiguous, mixing one row per order with one row per line item, so downstream sums double-count.
problem_solution.solution: A mart built to one explicit declared grain, with business-friendly column names, that consumers can trust as the entity's definitional table.
known_pitfalls: grain drift where a join fans out rows unexpectedly
leaking staging column names into the business layer
success_signals: one row per declared grain key
consumers query the mart directly without extra joins

blackbox.does: Compiles an ephemeral model into an inlined common table expression within each dependent model instead of building any relation, and returns a compile receipt with no persisted object.

problem_solution.problem: Small reusable transformation steps that only exist to be composed into other models do not warrant their own persisted relation cluttering the warehouse.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent materializes every helper step as a table, so the warehouse fills with thin intermediate relations no consumer queries directly.
problem_solution.solution: An ephemeral materialization that compiles the model SQL into a CTE inlined into each dependent model, keeping the logic reusable without creating a database object.
known_pitfalls: referencing an ephemeral model from a test that needs a relation
deep ephemeral chains producing unwieldy compiled SQL
success_signals: no database object is created for the model
dependents compile with the logic inlined as a CTE

blackbox.does: Materializes a model incrementally, building the full table on first run and thereafter applying only new or changed rows under the configured strategy, and returns a materialization receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Large append-heavy or slowly-updating models are wasteful to rebuild in full each run, so only the recent delta should be processed after the first build.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent chooses incremental but omits the is-incremental guard, so every run rebuilds fully, or the first run has no full-build path and starts empty.
problem_solution.solution: An incremental materialization that builds the whole table when the relation is absent and otherwise processes only the delta selected by the incremental predicate and strategy.
known_pitfalls: missing is-incremental guard causing full rebuilds
no full-build branch on first run
schema change on the source breaking the incremental append
success_signals: the first run builds the full table
later runs process only the delta and stay consistent

blackbox.does: Materializes a model as a physical table by recomputing the full result and replacing the relation, so reads are served from persisted rows, and returns a materialization receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Heavy models queried often by many consumers should pay their compute cost once at build time rather than on every read through a view.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves an expensive model as a view, so every dashboard load re-runs the heavy logic and query latency and warehouse load stay high.
problem_solution.solution: A table materialization that recomputes the full result on each build and replaces the relation, so consumers read persisted rows until the next scheduled build.
known_pitfalls: reads seeing data as stale as the last build
rebuilding a very large table when incremental would fit
success_signals: consumers read persisted rows without recomputing logic
the table matches the source as of the last build

blackbox.does: Materializes a model as a database view, replacing the view definition so each query recomputes the model SQL against current upstream data, and returns a materialization receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Lightweight models that must always reflect the latest upstream data and are cheap to compute should not be persisted as tables that go stale between runs.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent materializes a thin passthrough as a table, so it holds stale data until the next run and consumers see yesterday's numbers.
problem_solution.solution: A view materialization that stores only the model SQL, so every read recomputes against current upstream data with no storage of its own.
known_pitfalls: a view over heavy logic recomputing on every read
deeply nested views degrading query planning
success_signals: reads reflect current upstream data
no data is persisted for the model itself

blackbox.does: Defines a metric over a model by declaring its measure, aggregation, and allowed dimensions so downstream tools compute it consistently, and returns the metric set and a contract report.

problem_solution.problem: The same business metric is redefined slightly differently in each dashboard and query, so revenue or active-users numbers disagree across the organization.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a metric's aggregation inline in one dashboard, so the next team codes a subtly different version and the two never reconcile.
problem_solution.solution: A metric definition that declares the measure, aggregation, and permitted dimensions once against a model, giving every consumer one governed way to compute it.
known_pitfalls: a metric definition that drifts from its filters over time
success_signals: consumers compute the metric from one definition
the same metric reconciles across tools

blackbox.does: Enforces a model's declared output contract at build time, checking column names, data types, and constraints against the built relation and failing the build on any mismatch.

problem_solution.problem: Consumers depend on a model's column names and types, but an ordinary logic change can silently drop a column or change a type and break them downstream.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent refactors a model and changes a column's type without noticing, so a dependent model or BI tool breaks only when it next runs.
problem_solution.solution: A model contract that declares the expected column names, types, and constraints and is enforced at build time, failing the build before an incompatible shape ships.
known_pitfalls: a contract that drifts behind the intended output shape
constraint support that varies by warehouse
success_signals: a shape change that breaks the contract fails the build
the built relation matches the declared contract

blackbox.does: Persists model and column descriptions into the warehouse as relation and column comments during the build so catalog and BI tools read them directly, returning a contract report.

problem_solution.problem: Descriptions in the dbt catalog are invisible to warehouse-native catalog and BI tools that read comments directly from the database.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent documents models only in the dbt docs site, so analysts browsing the warehouse catalog see undocumented columns and re-ask what each means.
problem_solution.solution: A persist-docs step that writes the model and column descriptions into warehouse comments during the build, so native tooling surfaces the same documentation.
known_pitfalls: comment support that varies by warehouse
comments left stale when descriptions change
success_signals: warehouse comments match the model descriptions
re-persisting the same descriptions changes nothing

blackbox.does: Resolves a model reference to its fully qualified relation in the active target at compile time and records the resulting dependency edge in the lineage graph.

problem_solution.problem: Model SQL must depend on other models by logical name so the correct database, schema, and environment are substituted at build time and the DAG is derived automatically.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes fully qualified table names into model SQL, so dbt cannot see the dependency, builds in the wrong order, and lineage is blank.
problem_solution.solution: A ref resolver that maps a logical model name to its physical relation in the current target and emits the dependency edge that orders the build and populates lineage.
known_pitfalls: hard-coded relations that hide dependencies from the DAG
environment-specific names leaking into shared SQL
success_signals: the build order follows the resolved dependency edges
lineage shows the edge for every ref

blackbox.does: Reconciles the row count of a built model against its source-side expected count under a tolerance and returns a reconciliation report flagging any variance beyond tolerance.

problem_solution.problem: A transformation that unexpectedly drops or duplicates rows can pass column-level tests while quietly losing or inflating data volume.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent checks column values but never compares source and target counts, so a bad join that halves the rows passes every test.
problem_solution.solution: A reconciliation that computes the expected count from the source under the model's known filtering and compares it to the built row count within a declared tolerance.
known_pitfalls: a tolerance so wide it hides real loss
ignoring intended filtering when computing the expected count
success_signals: target count matches the expected count within tolerance
an unexpected drop or fan-out is flagged

blackbox.does: Runs configured pre-hook or post-hook SQL around a model or run (such as setting a session parameter or running a maintenance statement) and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Some operations must run in the warehouse around a model build - setting a session variable, applying a maintenance statement, or recording an audit row - not inside the model SQL itself.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent runs these statements manually and out of band, so they are forgotten in some environments and the build behaves differently across targets.
problem_solution.solution: A hook that attaches pre or post SQL to the model or run so the framework executes it in the right order on every build, keeping side operations reproducible.
known_pitfalls: a non-idempotent hook that errors on the second run
long-running maintenance in a hook blocking the build
hooks with side effects that are hard to audit
success_signals: the hook runs in the right order every build
re-running the hook is safe and produces the same state

blackbox.does: Loads a small version-controlled CSV seed file into a warehouse table with declared column types, replacing the prior contents, and returns a run receipt with the loaded row count.

problem_solution.problem: Small reference lookups (country codes, category maps, thresholds) belong in version control and must land as a typed table models can join to.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inserts reference values inline in SQL or lets types be inferred loosely, so a numeric code loads as text and joins silently miss.
problem_solution.solution: A seed load that reads a committed CSV, applies a declared per-column type contract, and replaces the seed table so the version-controlled file is the single source.
known_pitfalls: large data misused as a seed instead of a source
seed table drifting from the committed file
success_signals: loaded row count equals the CSV row count
column types match the declared contract

blackbox.does: Runs a hand-written singular test query that selects rows violating a specific business rule and passes only when the query returns zero rows, returning a test receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Some data assertions are specific to one model and one business rule that no reusable generic test expresses, yet still must fail the run when violated.
