problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes a bespoke check as a comment or an ad-hoc query it forgets to run, so the rule is never enforced in the pipeline.
problem_solution.solution: A singular test expressed as a SQL query that returns the offending rows; the framework fails the test when the row count is nonzero, wiring the rule into every run.
known_pitfalls: a query written to return passing rows instead of failing ones
a test that never actually runs in the suite
success_signals: the test fails when the rule is violated
zero returned rows means the assertion holds

blackbox.does: Captures type-2 slowly changing dimension history by detecting changed records against the current snapshot and closing prior versions while opening new ones, returning a merge receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Dimensions whose attributes change over time need their history preserved so facts can be analyzed against the attribute values that were in effect at event time.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites the dimension in place on each load, so historical attribute values are lost and time-based analysis silently uses today's values.
problem_solution.solution: A type-2 snapshot that compares incoming rows to the current version per key, closes the superseded version with an end timestamp, and inserts the new version as current.
known_pitfalls: overlapping validity windows for one key
more than one current row per key
success_signals: exactly one current row per key
re-running the same snapshot opens no new versions

blackbox.does: Declares a source relation with its database, schema, table name, and column metadata so downstream models reference it by name and its shape is documented and testable.

problem_solution.problem: Downstream models must depend on raw landing tables through a stable, documented handle rather than fully qualified names scattered across the project.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hard-codes raw database and schema names in model SQL, so a warehouse rename or environment switch breaks lineage and every dependent model.
problem_solution.solution: A source declaration that names the relation once with its location and column contract, giving every model a single indirection point and a place to attach tests and freshness.
known_pitfalls: hard-coded raw names bypassing the source handle
source column list drifting from the actual landing table
success_signals: models reference the source by name, not raw location
the declared columns match the landing table

blackbox.does: Checks how stale a source relation is by comparing the max loaded-at timestamp to warn and error thresholds and returns a freshness report with the observed lag per source.

problem_solution.problem: Pipelines silently serve stale data when an upstream load stops, and consumers only notice when a dashboard looks wrong days later.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent runs models on schedule without checking source freshness, so a stalled ingest is transformed into confidently stale marts.
problem_solution.solution: A freshness check that reads the max loaded-at timestamp per source and compares the lag to warn and error thresholds, failing the run before stale data propagates.
known_pitfalls: a loaded-at column that reflects transform time, not load time
timezone mismatches inflating or hiding lag
success_signals: a stalled source trips the error threshold
the observed lag matches the true load delay

blackbox.does: Builds a staging model that renames, casts, and lightly cleans one raw source relation into a typed, one-to-one staging table and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Raw source relations carry vendor column names, string-typed numbers, and inconsistent casing that every downstream model would otherwise re-clean independently.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent queries the raw table directly from a mart, hard-coding vendor column names and re-doing casts, so a source rename breaks every consumer at once.
problem_solution.solution: A one-to-one staging layer that standardizes names and types once, keeps the same grain as the source, and gives downstream models a stable typed interface.
known_pitfalls: joining or aggregating inside staging and losing the source grain
silent implicit casts that mask bad source data
dropping columns a downstream model still needs
success_signals: staging row count equals the source row count
downstream models reference only staging columns, never raw

blackbox.does: Resolves unselected model references against a prior-run manifest so a partial build can defer to already-built production relations instead of rebuilding the whole graph.

problem_solution.problem: Building only changed models in a slim CI run requires the unchanged upstream refs to point at existing production relations rather than being rebuilt.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent runs only the modified models but leaves their refs pointing at the empty CI schema, so the build fails on missing upstream relations.
problem_solution.solution: A defer resolver that reads a baseline manifest and rewrites references to unselected models so they read from the prior-built target while only selected models are built.
known_pitfalls: deferring to a stale baseline manifest
resolving a deferred ref to the wrong environment
success_signals: selected models build while unselected refs resolve to prod
no missing-relation errors in a slim build

blackbox.does: Generates deterministic surrogate keys by hashing the declared natural-key columns of a staging table and returns a stable natural-to-surrogate key map plus a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Facts and dimensions need a single stable join key derived from a possibly composite natural key, computed identically everywhere it is referenced.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent assigns incrementing row numbers as surrogates, so keys change every rebuild and facts join to the wrong dimension rows after a refresh.
problem_solution.solution: A deterministic hash of the ordered, null-normalized natural-key columns, producing the same surrogate for the same natural key on every run and across models.
known_pitfalls: null handling differences producing different hashes
column-order changes silently changing every key
success_signals: the same natural key hashes to the same surrogate every run
surrogate keys are unique across the entity

blackbox.does: Runs a model's transformation SQL against declared mock input rows and asserts the produced rows equal the declared expected rows, returning a test receipt with any diffs.

problem_solution.problem: Data tests validate real data, but the transformation logic itself - a case expression, a window, a parse - needs verification on controlled fixtures independent of production data.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent changes a case expression and relies on data tests over live data, so an edge case the current data never exercises ships broken.
problem_solution.solution: A unit test that feeds declared mock inputs through the model SQL and asserts the output matches expected rows exactly, exercising edge cases deterministically.
known_pitfalls: mock inputs that omit the boundary case being fixed
expected rows encoding the old buggy behavior
success_signals: the transformation produces the declared expected rows
an edge case regression fails the unit test

blackbox.does: Builds a wide one-big-table by joining a fact to its dimensions under a declared join policy, denormalizing attributes onto each fact row, and returns a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: BI tools and metric layers often want dimension attributes pre-joined onto the fact grain so analysts avoid re-deriving the same joins in every query.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent left-joins dimensions with a fan-out relationship and no join policy, so the wide table duplicates fact rows and inflates measures.
problem_solution.solution: A one-big-table that joins the fact to each dimension on the surrogate key under a declared one-to-one or many-to-one policy, preserving the fact grain and row count.
known_pitfalls: measure inflation after a many-to-many join
success_signals: wide row count equals the fact row count
measure totals match the source fact totals

blackbox.does: Appends new staging rows to a target table without touching existing rows, using an insert-only strategy and reconciling appended versus staged counts.

problem_solution.problem: Some tables grow purely by insertion and must never update or delete prior rows, yet loads still need protection against re-inserting the same staged batch.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent re-runs the load after a partial failure and appends the same rows twice because there is no batch-level insert guard.
problem_solution.solution: An insert-only writer that checks a batch marker before appending and reconciles the appended count so a re-run of an already-loaded batch adds nothing.
success_signals: re-loading a completed batch appends zero rows
existing rows are unchanged

blackbox.does: Reprocesses a bounded historical time window from the source into staging on demand, without disturbing the live watermark used by the ongoing incremental load.

problem_solution.problem: A historical correction requires reprocessing a specific past window, and it must not move or reset the live watermark that the normal incremental depends on.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent resets the shared watermark to run a backfill, so the ongoing incremental reprocesses everything after that point.
problem_solution.solution: A backfill that reads a bounded start-to-end window into staging as a separate run, leaving the live watermark untouched for the normal pipeline.
success_signals: the live watermark is unchanged by the backfill
only rows within the requested window are reprocessed

blackbox.does: Lands a raw source extract into an append-only bronze table verbatim, adding ingest audit columns and emitting a run receipt with the loaded row count.

problem_solution.problem: Raw source data must be captured into the lake exactly as received, with provenance columns, before any cleaning happens, so that reprocessing can always start from an untouched copy.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent transforms or filters rows during ingest, so the bronze layer no longer reflects the source and a later logic change cannot be replayed from raw.
problem_solution.solution: An append-only landing capability that copies the extract without semantic change, stamps load timestamp and batch id, and reconciles the written count against the source count.
success_signals: bronze row count equals source extract count
each row carries a batch id and load timestamp

blackbox.does: Consumes a streaming source in bounded micro-batches, appends each batch to the bronze table, and advances the stream position recorded in the run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: A continuous event stream must be persisted to the lake in bounded batches so that offsets advance monotonically and a restart resumes without gaps or double-counting.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent commits offsets before the write completes, so a crash between commit and write loses events that will never be re-read.
problem_solution.solution: A micro-batch loop that writes the batch first, records the max processed offset in the receipt, and only advances the committed position after a durable write.
success_signals: restart resumes at the last durable offset
no gap between committed offset and written rows

blackbox.does: Applies a collapsed change set to a target table as an atomic merge, inserting new keys, updating changed keys, and deleting tombstoned keys, and emits a merge receipt.

problem_solution.problem: A captured change set must be reflected in the target so that the target converges to the source, including physically removing rows for delete operations.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies inserts and updates but ignores deletes, so the target keeps rows that were removed at the source.
problem_solution.solution: An atomic merge keyed on the business key that inserts, updates, and deletes per operation type and reports counts by operation, idempotent on the same change set.
known_pitfalls: non-atomic apply leaving a partial state
success_signals: re-applying the same change set changes no rows
the target matches the source after apply

blackbox.does: Takes a one-time consistent full snapshot of a source table to seed a target before the ongoing change stream is applied, recording the snapshot boundary position.

problem_solution.problem: Before applying an incremental change stream, the target must be seeded with a full consistent copy of the source and the exact log position of that copy must be known.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent snapshots the source and starts the stream from now, leaving a gap of changes that happened during the snapshot.
problem_solution.solution: A bootstrap that reads a consistent full snapshot at a pinned source position and records that boundary so the stream resumes exactly where the snapshot ended.
known_pitfalls: gap between snapshot and stream start
success_signals: the stream resumes at the recorded snapshot boundary
no change is lost or double-applied across the handoff

blackbox.does: Reads inserts, updates, and deletes from a source change log or high-water comparison and emits an ordered change set of typed operations with before and after images.

problem_solution.problem: Downstream tables must track source inserts, updates, and deletes, so the source changes have to be captured as an ordered, typed change set rather than re-read in full.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent captures only inserts and updates and misses deletes, so removed source rows live on forever downstream.
problem_solution.solution: A capture that reads the change log or diffs against a high-water mark, emits typed operations with ordering metadata, and records the captured range.
known_pitfalls: gaps when the log is truncated
success_signals: deletes appear as typed operations in the change set
the captured position advances without gaps

blackbox.does: Orders a change set by its commit sequence and collapses multiple operations per key down to the single net latest operation, ready for a one-pass apply.

problem_solution.problem: A change set can contain several operations for the same key within one batch, and applying them out of order would leave the target in a wrong final state.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies changes in arrival order, so an update landing after a later delete resurrects a row that should be gone.
problem_solution.solution: An ordering and collapse step that sorts by commit sequence per key and keeps only the net latest operation so the apply is a single deterministic pass.
known_pitfalls: ties without a total sequence order
success_signals: one net operation remains per key
collapse is stable on re-run

blackbox.does: Advances the stored watermark to the maximum successfully processed change value only after a load commits, so a failed load never moves the watermark forward.

problem_solution.problem: The watermark must move forward exactly to the last committed change so the next extract neither reprocesses old rows nor skips uncommitted ones.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent advances the watermark before the load commits, so a subsequent failure loses every row between the old and new watermark.
problem_solution.solution: A commit-ordered advance that computes the max processed value from the committed batch and only then persists the new watermark, recording old and new values.
success_signals: watermark only advances after a durable load
a failed load leaves the watermark unchanged

blackbox.does: Validates a staging table against a data contract covering schema, nullability, ranges, and allowed values, passing conforming rows and reporting every violation.

problem_solution.problem: A producer and consumer agree on a contract, and every load must be checked against it so violations are caught at the boundary rather than downstream.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent checks only column names and lets out-of-range or null-in-required values pass, so bad data corrupts downstream models.
problem_solution.solution: A contract enforcer that checks schema, nullability, ranges, and enumerations, admits conforming rows, and emits a violation report by rule.
success_signals: only conforming rows reach silver
every violation is reported with its rule

blackbox.does: Derives a versioned data contract from a table and a schema spec, capturing columns, types, nullability, and key constraints so consumers can validate against it.

problem_solution.problem: Consumers need an explicit, versioned contract for a producer table, yet contracts are often stale documents that drift from the table they describe.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hand-writes a contract that omits nullability and keys, so consumers validate against an incomplete shape and still break.
problem_solution.solution: A publisher that reads the table plus schema spec and emits a versioned contract with columns, types, nullability, and keys as an artifact.
success_signals: the published contract matches the current table shape
each publish carries a distinct version

blackbox.does: Re-validates quarantined rows after a fix and merges the now-conforming rows into the target, leaving still-failing rows in quarantine with an incremented attempt count.

problem_solution.problem: Rows quarantined for a fixable reason must be retried after the fix and merged in, without reprocessing rows that still fail or double-applying ones that pass.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent re-runs the whole quarantine and re-merges rows that were already recovered on a prior pass, duplicating them.
problem_solution.solution: A reprocess that re-validates quarantined rows, merges the passing ones idempotently, and increments an attempt counter on those that still fail.
known_pitfalls: losing the failure reason on retry
success_signals: recovered rows merge exactly once
still-failing rows remain quarantined with a higher attempt count

blackbox.does: Collapses duplicate rows sharing a business key down to one survivor per key chosen by a deterministic tie-break order, and reports how many duplicates were removed.

problem_solution.problem: A staging feed contains multiple rows per business key and exactly one deterministic survivor must be kept so downstream joins do not fan out.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses distinct or an arbitrary group-by that keeps a nondeterministic row, so the survivor changes run to run and results are unstable.
problem_solution.solution: A dedupe that ranks rows within each key by an explicit tie-break order and keeps rank one, reporting removed counts so the choice is stable and auditable.
known_pitfalls: removing rows that differ on unkeyed columns
success_signals: exactly one row remains per business key
the same survivor is chosen on every re-run

blackbox.does: Refreshes a bounded set of partitions by deleting their existing rows and inserting the freshly computed rows in one transaction, replacing only the targeted partitions.

problem_solution.problem: When a recomputation can change many rows within known partitions, those partitions must be fully replaced without disturbing partitions outside the refresh window.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deletes the whole table before inserting, wiping partitions that were not part of the refresh window.
problem_solution.solution: A scoped delete-then-insert bounded to the target partitions inside one transaction, so only those partitions are replaced and the rest are untouched.
success_signals: only the targeted partitions change
re-running the refresh yields the same partition contents

blackbox.does: Merges a change set while deduplicating on an idempotency key recorded in the target so that redelivered or replayed operations are applied at most once.

problem_solution.problem: At-least-once delivery means the same operation can arrive more than once, and the merge must apply each unique operation exactly one time.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent merges every delivered operation, so a redelivered event is applied twice and a counter or balance drifts.
problem_solution.solution: A merge that records each applied operation's idempotency key in the target and skips any operation whose key is already present.
success_signals: redelivering an operation applies it zero additional times
each idempotency key appears once in the target

blackbox.does: Explodes nested JSON objects and arrays from a bronze column into typed relational rows and columns according to a schema spec, preserving a path back to the source row.

problem_solution.problem: Nested payloads landed in bronze must be flattened into typed columns and exploded array rows so downstream models can query them relationally without parsing JSON.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent flattens only the top level and drops nested arrays, silently losing repeated child records.
problem_solution.solution: A structured flattener that walks the declared paths, explodes arrays into child rows keyed to the parent, and keeps a source path so the collapse is reversible.
known_pitfalls: orphaned child rows without a parent link
success_signals: re-nesting the flattened output reproduces the source structure
child rows all resolve to a parent

blackbox.does: Pre-aggregates additive measures from a detailed silver table up to a coarser reporting grain, producing one summarized row per group with reconciled measure totals.

problem_solution.problem: Dashboards over billions of detail rows are slow, so an aggregate at a coarser grain must be maintained whose totals still tie out to the detail.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sums a semi-additive or non-additive measure across a dimension where that is invalid, producing inflated totals.
problem_solution.solution: A rollup that groups to the declared grain, aggregates only measures valid for that grain, and reconciles the aggregate totals against the detail.
known_pitfalls: double counting from a fan-out join
grain not covering the group-by keys
success_signals: aggregate totals tie to the detail totals
exactly one row per group key

blackbox.does: Assembles business-ready gold tables from conformed silver inputs at a declared grain, applying business rules and derived measures for direct consumption by reporting.

problem_solution.problem: Reporting needs curated, business-rule-applied tables at a stated grain, built from trustworthy silver inputs rather than each dashboard re-deriving logic from raw.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent builds the gold table straight from bronze, re-implementing cleaning and business rules that then drift from the shared definitions.
problem_solution.solution: A curate step that consumes conformed silver at the declared grain, applies business rules once, and enforces one row per grain key.
known_pitfalls: business logic diverging from shared definitions
success_signals: exactly one row per grain key
reporting reads gold without further transformation

blackbox.does: Derives hidden partition values from source columns using declared transforms such as day-of-timestamp or bucket-of-key, so writers partition without exposing extra columns.

problem_solution.problem: Partitioning should follow a transform of a source column, but forcing queries to filter on a separate derived column is error-prone and easy to forget.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent materializes a redundant partition column and queries that filter only the base column then fail to prune.
problem_solution.solution: A hidden partition transform that derives the partition value from the base column via a declared function so queries filtering the base column still prune.
known_pitfalls: transform mismatch between write and read
success_signals: queries filtering the base column prune correctly
the same input maps to the same partition value

blackbox.does: Expires table snapshots older than a retention threshold and removes the metadata and data files they alone referenced, keeping the newest snapshots reachable.

problem_solution.problem: Snapshot history grows without bound, so old snapshots must be expired to control metadata size while keeping recent versions available for time travel.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent expires snapshots more recent than the retention threshold, destroying versions that rollback or audits still need.
problem_solution.solution: A snapshot expiry that keeps snapshots newer than the threshold, removes only files uniquely referenced by expired snapshots, and reports what was expired.
known_pitfalls: removing files shared with a retained snapshot
success_signals: snapshots newer than the threshold remain reachable
current table contents are unchanged

blackbox.does: Upserts staging rows into a target keyed on a unique business key, inserting new keys and updating existing ones so that re-running the same batch leaves the target unchanged.

problem_solution.problem: A load must be safe to retry after a partial failure, so applying the same staging batch twice must produce exactly the same target as applying it once.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inserts unconditionally, so a retry duplicates every row because there is no key-based match on the target.
problem_solution.solution: An upsert keyed on the unique business key that updates matched rows and inserts unmatched rows, making a repeat of the same batch a no-op.
known_pitfalls: non-unique merge key updating many rows
partial upsert leaving a mixed state
success_signals: re-running the same batch changes zero rows
each business key appears once in the target

blackbox.does: Runs a dbt-style incremental build that filters to new source rows since the last run, deduplicates on the unique key, and merges only the new keys into the target.

problem_solution.problem: An incremental model must process only rows arrived since the last run and still keep exactly one row per unique key when a source resends a record.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent filters incrementally but skips dedupe, so a resent record produces two rows for the same key in the incremental target.
problem_solution.solution: An incremental strategy that selects new rows by the incremental predicate, deduplicates within the batch, and merges on the unique key.
success_signals: one row per unique key after each incremental run
re-running the same window changes no rows

blackbox.does: Atomically overwrites the specific partitions present in the staging batch with the staged rows, leaving all other partitions of the target untouched.

problem_solution.problem: A recompute produces the full contents of certain partitions and must swap them in atomically, without a dynamic overwrite accidentally clearing unrelated partitions.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent runs a static overwrite that replaces the entire table when only a few partitions were recomputed.
problem_solution.solution: A dynamic partition overwrite scoped to the partition values present in the batch, swapping just those partitions in one atomic operation.
known_pitfalls: static overwrite clearing the whole table
partitions in the batch not matching the target scheme
success_signals: only partitions present in the batch are replaced
re-running the same batch yields identical partitions

blackbox.does: Merges records that arrived after their event-time partition was built into the correct historical partitions, updating affected aggregates and reporting touched partitions.

problem_solution.problem: Events sometimes arrive after their event-time partition has already been processed, so they must be routed to the correct past partition rather than the arrival day.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes late events into the current partition by processing time, so historical partitions and their aggregates stay wrong.
problem_solution.solution: A reconcile that keys late rows by event time, merges them into the correct historical partitions, and recomputes the affected partition aggregates.
known_pitfalls: placing late rows by arrival time
double-counting a late row on re-run
success_signals: late rows land in their event-time partition
re-running the reconcile changes no counts

blackbox.does: Records the upstream inputs, transform identity, and produced outputs of a model run as a lineage receipt so downstream impact and provenance can be traced.

problem_solution.problem: When a column is wrong, teams need to know which inputs and transform produced it and what depends on it, which requires captured lineage per run.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves lineage implicit in code, so tracing a bad value means manually reading every model to guess its inputs.
problem_solution.solution: A lineage capture that records the run's declared inputs, transform id, and outputs into a receipt, building a traceable input-to-output graph.
success_signals: every output traces to its declared inputs
the receipt matches the inputs the run actually read

blackbox.does: Rewrites and compacts a table's metadata manifests so planning reads fewer manifest files, without moving or changing any underlying data file.

problem_solution.problem: Frequent commits fragment table metadata into many manifest files, slowing query planning even when the data files themselves are fine.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent rewrites data files to fix planning cost when only the metadata manifests were fragmented, doing far more work than needed.
problem_solution.solution: A metadata-only manifest rewrite that compacts manifest files and leaves every data file and row untouched, recording manifest counts before and after.
success_signals: no data file is moved or changed
planning reads fewer manifests after the rewrite

blackbox.does: Executes a single atomic merge-into statement matching source to target on a key, applying matched updates and unmatched inserts in one transaction with a merge receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Update and insert must be applied atomically against a large target so a reader never sees a half-applied batch and the merge key does not match multiple targets.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent runs a delete then an insert in two statements, so a concurrent reader between them sees the target missing rows.
problem_solution.solution: A single merge-into that matches on the key and applies updates and inserts atomically, guarded against a source key matching more than one target row.
known_pitfalls: source key matching multiple target rows
success_signals: the merge applies in one atomic commit
re-running the merge changes no rows

blackbox.does: Aligns two source record sets onto a common schema and unions them into a single record set, tagging each row with its origin and reconciling the combined count.

problem_solution.problem: Two feeds that describe the same entity in different shapes must be combined into one table with a shared schema and a preserved record of which feed each row came from.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent unions mismatched columns positionally, so values land in the wrong fields and the origin of each row is lost.
problem_solution.solution: A schema-aligning union that maps each source to the shared columns by name, tags origin, and reconciles the output count against the sum of inputs.
success_signals: output count equals sum of input counts
every row carries a valid origin tag

blackbox.does: Permanently removes data files no longer referenced by any snapshot within the retention window, reclaiming storage and reporting the files deleted.

problem_solution.problem: Old unreferenced files accumulate and must be removed to reclaim storage, but deleting files still inside the retention window breaks time travel and readers.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent vacuums with a zero retention window and deletes files a concurrent long-running reader still needs, causing read failures.
problem_solution.solution: A vacuum that only removes files unreferenced by any live snapshot and older than the retention window, reporting deleted files and honoring the minimum retention.
known_pitfalls: deleting files still referenced by a snapshot
success_signals: current table contents are unchanged
only unreferenced, out-of-retention files are removed

blackbox.does: Applies a new partition specification to an existing table so future writes use the new layout while existing data remains readable under its original partitioning.

problem_solution.problem: As data volume grows the partition layout must change, but existing partitions cannot be rewritten cheaply and queries must still read across both layouts.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent rewrites the whole table to change partitioning, incurring a full rewrite and a long outage instead of evolving the spec.
problem_solution.solution: A partition-spec evolution that registers the new spec for future writes while old files keep their original spec, so reads span both transparently.
known_pitfalls: queries that cannot span two specs
success_signals: existing data stays readable under its original spec
new writes use the new spec

blackbox.does: Computes which table partitions a query predicate can safely skip from catalog statistics and partition metadata, producing a prune plan without reading data files.

problem_solution.problem: A query should read only the partitions its predicate can match, so a prune plan must identify skippable partitions from metadata before any data is scanned.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent reads all partitions because the predicate is not mapped to partition columns, scanning far more than necessary.
problem_solution.solution: A pruning planner that maps predicates to partition columns, uses partition statistics to mark non-matching partitions skippable, and emits the plan.
known_pitfalls: predicate not aligned to partition columns
success_signals: only partitions that can match remain in the plan
no matching partition is pruned

blackbox.does: Applies deterministic masking, hashing, or tokenization to the sensitive columns named in a data contract, producing a protected table and a report of masked fields.

problem_solution.problem: Sensitive columns must be masked before data reaches broad-access layers, and the masking must be deterministic so joins on the masked key still work.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies a random or salted-per-run hash, so the same identity masks to different values across tables and can no longer be joined.
problem_solution.solution: A contract-driven masker that applies a stable transform to each declared sensitive column and reports which fields were masked and by which method.
success_signals: the same input value masks to the same output every run
every contract-listed field is masked

blackbox.does: Splits a staging table against a contract into a passing set and a quarantine set, tagging each quarantined row with its failed rule so the good data keeps flowing.

problem_solution.problem: A few bad rows should not fail an entire load, so violating rows must be diverted to a quarantine with their reason while valid rows proceed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent fails the whole batch on the first bad row, blocking good data, or drops bad rows with no record of why.
problem_solution.solution: A split that routes conforming rows onward and diverts violating rows to a quarantine table tagged with the failed rule and count by rule.
known_pitfalls: failing the whole batch on one bad row
dropping bad rows without a reason
success_signals: passing plus quarantined equals the input count
each quarantined row carries its failed rule

blackbox.does: Left-joins staging rows to a governed reference lookup to add descriptive attributes, routing unmatched keys to an unknown member rather than dropping the rows.

problem_solution.problem: Fact-shaped rows must be enriched with attributes from a reference table without inflating or losing rows when a lookup key is missing or non-unique.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inner-joins to the reference and drops every row whose key is absent, and a duplicate reference key fans the rows out.
problem_solution.solution: A left join against a uniqueness-checked reference that substitutes an unknown member for missing keys and reconciles input and output counts.
known_pitfalls: duplicate reference key fanning out rows
null attributes not mapped to unknown member
success_signals: input and output row counts reconcile
unmatched keys resolve to the unknown member

blackbox.does: Re-reads a stream from a supplied starting offset and re-lands the events, using an event idempotency key so already-present events are not duplicated on replay.

problem_solution.problem: After a logic fix or data loss, a stream must be reprocessed from a known offset without creating duplicate rows for events that were already landed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent replays from an offset and blindly appends, doubling every event that had already been ingested past that point.
problem_solution.solution: A replay reader that seeks to the offset and lands events through an idempotency-key guard so re-seen events are skipped rather than duplicated.
success_signals: replaying a covered range adds no new rows
the replayed offset range is recorded in the receipt

blackbox.does: Compares row counts between a source and a target set at the whole-table and per-partition level and reports any discrepancy beyond the configured tolerance.

problem_solution.problem: A load can silently lose or duplicate rows, so source and target counts must be reconciled overall and per partition to detect drift early.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent compares only total counts, so a partition that gained rows and another that lost the same number net to zero and hide the error.
problem_solution.solution: A reconciliation that compares counts at the table and partition grain, flags any per-partition gap past tolerance, and reports the differences.
known_pitfalls: ignoring partition-level offsets that net out
success_signals: per-partition counts reconcile within tolerance
any discrepancy is reported with its partition

blackbox.does: Applies an additive, backward-compatible schema change such as a new nullable column or a widened type, and reports the change while rejecting breaking alterations.

problem_solution.problem: Source schemas change over time and the table must absorb additive changes automatically while blocking changes that would break existing readers.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent applies any incoming schema change, including a narrowing type or dropped column, and silently breaks downstream consumers.
problem_solution.solution: An evolution applier that permits additive and widening changes, refuses narrowing or drops without review, and reports every change it applied.
known_pitfalls: dropping a column readers depend on
success_signals: existing readers keep working after the change
breaking changes are rejected with a reason

blackbox.does: Transforms raw bronze rows into a cleaned, typed, conformed silver table by casting types, trimming and standardizing values, and applying the declared naming and null rules.

problem_solution.problem: Bronze data carries source quirks, inconsistent types, and raw naming that must be normalized once into a trustworthy silver layer that every downstream model can rely on.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hard-codes cleaning inline in many downstream models, so the same field is cleaned differently in each place and the results disagree.
problem_solution.solution: A single conform step that casts types, standardizes values, applies naming and null policy, and reconciles the row count so cleaning is defined exactly once.
known_pitfalls: losing rows to overly strict filters
success_signals: all downstream models read one conformed field definition
row count reconciles with bronze minus documented drops

blackbox.does: Projects and coerces a bronze table onto an exact target column set, order, and types defined by a schema spec, reporting any columns added, dropped, or coerced.

problem_solution.problem: Downstream consumers require a stable column set and types, so an upstream table must be conformed to an agreed schema and any deviation must be surfaced rather than passed through.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent select-stars the source, so a new upstream column silently flows downstream and breaks a consumer expecting a fixed shape.
problem_solution.solution: A conform step that projects to the declared columns in order, coerces types, and emits a report of every add, drop, and coercion it applied.
success_signals: output shape matches the schema spec exactly
every deviation appears in the contract report

blackbox.does: Rewrites many small data files within targeted partitions into fewer right-sized files, preserving the exact row set and reporting the file count before and after.

problem_solution.problem: Streaming and frequent loads produce many tiny files that slow reads, so files must be compacted into larger ones without changing any row.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent rewrites files but reorders or drops rows, so the compacted table no longer matches the original contents.
problem_solution.solution: A bin-packing compaction that rewrites small files into target-sized files within a partition scope, verifying the row set is byte-for-value identical.
known_pitfalls: target file size mismatched to reads
success_signals: row set is unchanged after compaction
re-running compaction rewrites nothing

blackbox.does: Reads a table as of a single consistent table version so a multi-statement job sees a stable snapshot even while concurrent writers commit new versions.

problem_solution.problem: A job that issues several reads must see one consistent version of a table, otherwise a writer committing mid-job yields a result mixing two states.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent issues repeated reads without pinning a version, so a concurrent commit changes the data between reads and the outputs disagree.
problem_solution.solution: A read that pins the current table version or a requested snapshot id up front and serves every read of the job from that fixed version.
success_signals: all reads in the job resolve to one version id
the served version is recorded in the receipt

blackbox.does: Applies delete operations from a change set as a soft delete, setting a deleted flag and delete timestamp on matched rows rather than physically removing them.

problem_solution.problem: Deletes must be reflected while keeping history queryable, so removed keys should be flagged deleted rather than dropped, without hiding still-active rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites the whole row on a soft delete and loses the prior attribute values that history queries still need.
problem_solution.solution: A soft-delete merge that sets a deleted flag and timestamp on matched keys, preserves the last attribute values, and is idempotent on the same deletes.
known_pitfalls: not filtering deleted rows in active views
success_signals: deleted rows carry a flag and timestamp
re-applying the same deletes flips no additional rows

blackbox.does: Measures the age of the newest loaded record against warn and error thresholds and reports whether a source is fresh, stale, or breached before dependent models run.

problem_solution.problem: Downstream models should not run on stale inputs, so the age of the newest source record must be checked against thresholds before builds proceed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent trusts that a source loaded and builds on data that is hours stale because a broken upstream job left it frozen.
problem_solution.solution: A freshness check that reads the newest load timestamp, compares it to warn and error thresholds, and reports a fresh, warn, or error status.
known_pitfalls: using load time instead of event time when required
success_signals: stale sources are flagged before dependents build
the reported age matches the newest record

blackbox.does: Creates a shallow metadata-only clone of a table that shares the source data files, giving an isolated writable copy for testing without duplicating storage.

problem_solution.problem: A safe isolated copy of a large table is needed for testing or a what-if, but physically duplicating the data is slow and wastes storage.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deep-copies every file to make a test copy, taking a long time and doubling storage for a throwaway.
problem_solution.solution: A shallow clone that copies only metadata and references the existing data files, giving an isolated version whose later writes do not affect the source.
known_pitfalls: clone writes leaking back to the source
source vacuum removing files the clone shares
success_signals: the clone reads identical contents to the source at clone time
writes to the clone do not change the source

blackbox.does: Restores a table to a prior snapshot or version as a new current version, reverting a bad write while retaining the intervening history for audit.

problem_solution.problem: A bad load can corrupt a table, and it must be reverted to a known-good prior version quickly without destroying the record of what happened in between.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent deletes rows manually to undo a bad load, guessing at what changed and leaving the table in a third, still-wrong state.
problem_solution.solution: A restore that sets the table's current version to a chosen prior snapshot as a new commit, so the revert is exact and the intervening history is preserved.
known_pitfalls: manual row surgery instead of restore
success_signals: current contents match the target version
the intervening history remains queryable

blackbox.does: Extracts only source rows whose change column exceeds the stored watermark, using an inclusive lower bound with overlap so boundary rows are never missed.

problem_solution.problem: Only rows changed since the last extract should be pulled, but a strict boundary can skip rows sharing the watermark timestamp under clock or commit skew.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent filters strictly greater than the watermark, so rows with the exact boundary timestamp are silently skipped forever.
problem_solution.solution: An extract with an inclusive lower bound and a small overlap window that re-pulls boundary rows, relying on a downstream dedupe to absorb the overlap.
success_signals: no changed row is skipped at the boundary
the extracted range is recorded in the receipt

blackbox.does: Reorganizes a table's data files to co-locate rows by high-cardinality filter columns using a clustering or z-order layout, preserving the row set exactly.

problem_solution.problem: Selective queries scan too many files because related rows are scattered, so files should be reorganized to cluster rows by the columns queries filter on.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent clusters on columns that are rarely filtered, adding rewrite cost while queries still scan everything.
problem_solution.solution: A layout optimize that clusters files by the declared high-cardinality filter columns, leaving the row set unchanged and recording the layout applied.
known_pitfalls: reordering that changes the row set
success_signals: row set is unchanged after optimize
files cluster on the declared columns

blackbox.does: Returns rows of the first set whose match key is absent from the second set (SQL WHERE NOT EXISTS), the anti-membership complement of a semi-join, with first-set cardinality preserved.

problem_solution.problem: You want first-set rows with NO match in the second set - unmatched, orphaned, or new records - without fan-out and without null-key false negatives.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses a left join with an IS NULL filter but mishandles null keys, so rows with null match keys wrongly appear or disappear.
problem_solution.solution: An anti-join that keeps first-set rows whose key is absent from the second set, handling null keys explicitly and preserving first-set columns.
known_pitfalls: using an inner join by mistake
duplicate keys in B changing results
success_signals: semi-join and anti-join partition A exactly
output is a subset of A

blackbox.does: Forms the Cartesian product of two record sets under an explicit size-guard policy that caps or rejects the output when the product would exceed a declared row budget.

problem_solution.problem: Some tasks genuinely need every pairing of two sets (grids, scenario matrices), but an unguarded Cartesian product can explode to an unusable size.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent issues a cross join with no size guard and materializes billions of rows, exhausting the warehouse.
problem_solution.solution: A guarded cross join that computes the expected product size against a declared budget and caps or rejects before materializing.
common_outputs: size within budget or explicit rejection
known_pitfalls: cross join hidden behind a missing join predicate
success_signals: output size equals the product of inputs
over-budget requests are rejected before materializing

blackbox.does: Unions a family of record sets and keeps one winning row per dedup key using a declared precedence (source priority or recency), idempotent under re-running on its own output.

problem_solution.problem: The same entity arrives in several source sets and must collapse to one winning row by a declared precedence, and re-running must not change the survivors.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent unions the sets and deduplicates arbitrarily, so which duplicate survives depends on scan order and changes run to run.
problem_solution.solution: A cross-set dedupe that unions the family and picks one row per key by an explicit precedence, yielding a unique-key idempotent result.
known_pitfalls: nondeterministic winner without an explicit precedence
success_signals: exactly one row per dedup key
re-running on the output changes nothing

blackbox.does: Returns the distinct rows in the first record set that are NOT in the second (SQL EXCEPT/MINUS), an order-sensitive operation bounded by the first input's cardinality.

problem_solution.problem: You need the rows in one set that are absent from another - for anti-membership, reconciliation, or 'what's new' - and direction matters.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent swaps the operands or uses an inner join instead of an anti-semantics, returning the wrong difference direction.
problem_solution.solution: An except step that returns distinct rows of the first set not found in the second, order-sensitive and bounded by the first input.
common_outputs: rows only in the first input
success_signals: output is a subset of the first input
rows in the second input never appear

blackbox.does: Returns the distinct rows present in BOTH schema-compatible record sets (SQL INTERSECT), a commutative operation whose output cardinality never exceeds the smaller input.

problem_solution.problem: You need only the rows two sets have in common, and the result must not exceed the smaller set or depend on operand order.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent emulates intersect with a join but mishandles duplicates or nulls, returning rows that are not truly in both sets.
problem_solution.solution: An intersect step that returns the distinct rows present in both sets, bounded by the smaller input and independent of operand order.
known_pitfalls: duplicate handling differing from INTERSECT semantics
success_signals: output cardinality does not exceed the smaller input
swapping operands yields the same set

blackbox.does: Annotates each row of the first set with a boolean flag indicating whether its key is present in the second set, preserving cardinality and adding one column.

problem_solution.problem: You want to keep every first-set row but mark which ones exist in a reference set, for downstream branching, without dropping or duplicating any rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins to the reference set to get the flag and fans out on duplicate reference keys, changing the row count.
problem_solution.solution: A membership-flag step that probes existence in the reference set and adds a boolean column while holding cardinality constant.
common_outputs: A with an added membership boolean
success_signals: output row count equals A's
the flag matches a semi-join membership exactly

blackbox.does: Unions an arbitrary family of schema-compatible record sets into one set in a single pass, validating that every member shares the common schema before concatenating.

problem_solution.problem: Many partitioned or per-source record sets must be combined into one, and folding pairwise is error-prone when a single member has a divergent schema.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent folds unions pairwise and lets one odd member's schema silently coerce the whole result, corrupting columns.
problem_solution.solution: An n-ary union that first validates every member against the common schema, then concatenates them in one pass.
common_outputs: row count equal to the member sum
known_pitfalls: one member with a divergent schema
success_signals: every member validated before concatenation
output count equals the sum of member counts

blackbox.does: Computes membership overlap statistics between two record sets on a match key - intersection size, each side's exclusive count, union size, and Jaccard overlap - without materializing the joined rows.

problem_solution.problem: Before joining or reconciling two sets you need to know how much they overlap on a key, but running the full join just to count is wasteful and can mislead on duplicates.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent estimates overlap from a fanned-out join count, over-counting when keys are non-unique.
problem_solution.solution: An overlap report that counts distinct keys per side and their intersection to report exclusive counts, union size, and Jaccard.
known_pitfalls: counting fanned-out join rows instead of distinct keys
success_signals: exclusive plus intersection equals each side's distinct count
Jaccard lies in zero to one

blackbox.does: Splits one record set into a family of disjoint subsets by a partition predicate or key so that the subsets are mutually exclusive and their union reconstructs the input exactly.

problem_solution.problem: A single set must be divided into subsets for parallel handling or routing, and the split must lose no rows and duplicate none - a true partition.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes overlapping filter predicates so some rows land in two subsets and others in none, and the parts no longer sum to the whole.
problem_solution.solution: A partition step whose predicate assigns each row to exactly one subset, verified so the subsets are disjoint and their union equals the input.
known_pitfalls: overlapping predicates assigning a row twice
subset row counts not summing to the input
success_signals: subset counts sum to the input count
unioning the subsets reproduces the input

blackbox.does: Reconciles two record sets to a common target schema - aligning column names, order, and types and filling missing columns with nulls - so a subsequent set operation is well-defined.

problem_solution.problem: Set operations require identical schemas, but real sources differ in column order, names, and types, so a pre-alignment step is needed before any union or intersect.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent unions mismatched sets directly and lets positional coercion put values in the wrong columns.
problem_solution.solution: A schema-align step that maps both sets onto a declared target schema, filling absent columns with nulls and coercing types safely, preserving row counts.
common_outputs: two sets sharing the target schema
known_pitfalls: filling a required column with nulls
success_signals: both outputs match the target schema exactly
row counts equal their inputs

blackbox.does: Returns rows of the first set whose match key appears in the second set (SQL WHERE EXISTS), never duplicating first-set rows regardless of how many second-set matches exist.

problem_solution.problem: You want to keep first-set rows that have a match in the second set without pulling second-set columns or fanning out on multiple matches.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses an inner join, so a first-set row with three matches appears three times and second-set columns leak in.
problem_solution.solution: A semi-join that filters the first set by existence of a matching key in the second, preserving first-set cardinality exactly.
common_outputs: no duplication and no B columns
known_pitfalls: using an inner join and fanning out
success_signals: output is a subset of A with A's exact columns
row count never exceeds A

blackbox.does: Returns rows in exactly one of two record sets - the union minus the intersection - a commutative operation useful for diffing two snapshots into added-plus-removed.

problem_solution.problem: Diffing two snapshots requires the rows present in exactly one side (added or removed), not those common to both.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent returns only additions or only removals, missing half the diff, or includes unchanged rows.
problem_solution.solution: A symmetric-difference step that emits union-minus-intersection, so both added and removed rows appear and unchanged rows do not.
known_pitfalls: losing which side a row came from
success_signals: no row common to both inputs appears
swapping operands yields the same set

blackbox.does: Concatenates two schema-compatible record sets into one multiset preserving duplicates (SQL UNION ALL), after checking column compatibility, so cardinality equals the sum of inputs.

problem_solution.problem: Two record sets with the same shape must be combined keeping every row, but only if their columns truly line up by name, type, and order.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent unions sets with mismatched column order so values land in the wrong columns, or silently drops duplicates it was meant to keep.
problem_solution.solution: A union-all step that validates schema compatibility, then concatenates preserving duplicates so output cardinality equals the input sum.
common_outputs: row count equal to the input sum
success_signals: output row count equals sum of inputs
columns align by name and type

blackbox.does: Unions two schema-compatible record sets and removes exact duplicate rows (SQL UNION), producing a set whose rows are distinct and idempotent under re-union with either input.

problem_solution.problem: Two overlapping record sets must be merged into a distinct set, and re-merging an already-merged set with either input must not change it.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent uses UNION ALL and forgets to deduplicate, so overlapping rows appear twice and downstream counts inflate.
problem_solution.solution: A union-distinct step that combines both sets and removes exact-duplicate rows, yielding an idempotent distinct set.
known_pitfalls: case or whitespace differences defeating dedup
cost of distinct on huge sets ignored
success_signals: re-union with either input leaves the set unchanged
no exact-duplicate rows remain

blackbox.does: Validates a dimension definition (name, key, attribute columns, and the join path back to fact grain) into a governed semantic-model entry so metrics can be sliced by it consistently.

problem_solution.problem: Slicing a metric by a dimension requires a known join path and attribute set, but those are re-invented per query so the same slice yields different joins and double-counts fanned-out rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins a dimension table without declaring its key grain, fanning out the fact rows and inflating additive measures.
problem_solution.solution: A definition step that records the dimension key, attributes, and the validated join path to fact grain so every metric slices it the same way.
known_pitfalls: joining at a finer grain than the dimension key
missing surrogate key on the dimension
attributes that belong to a different grain
success_signals: dimension key uniquely identifies its rows
slicing does not inflate additive measures

blackbox.does: Compiles a validated metric query plan into dialect-specific SQL with the correct aggregations, joins, group-by, and filters, deterministically for a given plan and dialect.

problem_solution.problem: The same metric query must become correct SQL for whatever warehouse dialect is in play, and the compilation must be reproducible so a plan always yields the same query.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes dialect-specific SQL by hand each time, so aggregations and quoting drift between engines and the output is not reproducible.
problem_solution.solution: A compile step that turns the resolved plan into dialect SQL from a single template set, keyed by plan and dialect, with a byte-stable result.
known_pitfalls: losing a plan filter during compilation
success_signals: same plan and dialect compile to identical SQL
compiled SQL references only planned tables

blackbox.does: Recomputes each governed metric two independent ways (definition-driven and a reference reconciliation query) and reports any metric whose totals disagree beyond a tolerance.

problem_solution.problem: A governed metric can drift from reality when its underlying marts change, and nothing detects that the definition and the physical data no longer agree.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent trusts the definition without ever reconciling it against an independent recomputation, so silent drift ships to dashboards.
problem_solution.solution: A check that recomputes each metric via its definition and via an independent reference query and flags disagreements beyond tolerance.
known_pitfalls: tolerance too loose to catch drift
reference query sharing the same bug as the definition
success_signals: disagreements are surfaced with the offending metric
clean metrics report exact agreement

blackbox.does: Validates a metric definition (name, aggregation, base measure, allowed grains, filters) into a governed semantic-model entry with a stable metric key, without touching any physical table.

problem_solution.problem: Business metrics like active users or net revenue are re-derived inconsistently in every dashboard, so two reports disagree on the same number because the aggregation, filters, or grain differ silently.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent writes ad-hoc SUM/COUNT SQL per dashboard, embedding filter logic inline, so no single governed definition exists and the same metric name means different math in different places.
problem_solution.solution: A definition step that captures the aggregation, base measure, allowed grains, and canonical filters once as a validated semantic-model entry keyed by a stable metric id.
known_pitfalls: embedding filters that should be query-time dimensions
allowing a grain the base measure cannot support
duplicate metric keys for the same concept
success_signals: metric key is stable across rebuilds
the same definition drives every consumer

blackbox.does: Joins two metric result sets on their shared conformed grain into one aligned result set, guarding against fan-out and preserving each metric at the requested grain.

problem_solution.problem: Two metrics computed separately must be compared side by side, but they only align if joined on a truly conformed grain, or the join fans out and corrupts both.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins two metric outputs on an approximately-matching key, fanning rows out and inflating both metrics.
problem_solution.solution: A conformed-join step that aligns two metric result sets on a declared shared grain and verifies the joined grain stays unique.
common_outputs: one row per shared grain key
known_pitfalls: grain of one metric finer than the other
nulls in the join key dropping rows
success_signals: joined grain key is unique
neither metric total changes after the join

title: Metric Query Plan

blackbox.does: Resolves a metric query (metrics, group-by dimensions, filters, grain) against the semantic model into a validated query plan, rejecting requests for unsupported grains or undefined metrics before any SQL runs.

problem_solution.problem: A consumer asks for metrics grouped by dimensions at a grain, but not every metric supports every grain, and unsupported combinations must fail early rather than return silently-wrong numbers.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent generates SQL for any requested grain, so a non-additive metric gets summed across an unsupported dimension and returns a plausible but wrong total.
problem_solution.solution: A planning step that validates each requested metric and dimension against the semantic model, checks grain compatibility, and emits a resolved plan or an explicit rejection.
known_pitfalls: allowing a non-additive metric at an unsupported grain
success_signals: unsupported grain requests are rejected, not answered wrongly
the plan names every table and join it will use

source_ref_families: query planning against a metric model

blackbox.does: End-to-end resolves a metric query against the semantic model and physical marts into a metric result set, planning, compiling, and executing under the governed definitions so the numbers match every other consumer.

problem_solution.problem: Consumers want a metric result set for a query, and it must equal what every other consumer would get for the same query so dashboards agree.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent runs bespoke SQL that bypasses the governed definitions, so its totals differ from the canonical metric and reconciliation fails.
problem_solution.solution: A resolve step that plans and compiles against the semantic model, executes, and returns a result set carrying the metric keys and grain it was computed at.
common_outputs: grain and metric keys on each row
known_pitfalls: bypassing governed definitions with raw SQL
returning a grain different from the request
double counting via a fan-out join
success_signals: result reconciles with the governed metric definition
same query returns the same totals across consumers

blackbox.does: Assembles validated metric and dimension entries plus their physical bindings into one semantic model and emits a queryable metric catalog with resolvable metric/dimension keys.

problem_solution.problem: Metrics, dimensions, and their physical table bindings live in scattered files, so a consumer cannot discover what is queryable or how a metric maps to real columns.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hardcodes table and column names in each query, so when a mart is renamed every consumer breaks and nothing lists the available metrics.
problem_solution.solution: An assembly step that binds validated metrics and dimensions to physical marts and emits a single catalog whose keys are the only interface consumers touch.
known_pitfalls: dangling binding to a nonexistent column
two metrics bound to conflicting grains
success_signals: every catalog metric resolves to a real column
consumers reference keys, never raw tables

blackbox.does: Builds and updates an accumulating-snapshot fact with one row per pipeline instance whose milestone dates and lag measures are revised in place as the process advances.

problem_solution.problem: A workflow with defined milestones, such as an order moving from placed to shipped to delivered, is best tracked as one evolving row updated as each milestone completes.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inserts a new row at each milestone instead of updating the existing one, so a single instance spreads across many partial rows.
problem_solution.solution: An accumulating-snapshot capability that upserts one row per instance, filling the milestone date and lag columns as each step occurs.
known_pitfalls: a new row per milestone instead of an update
lag measures not recomputed on update
success_signals: one row per pipeline instance
re-applying a milestone event changes nothing

blackbox.does: Builds an aggregate fact by rolling an atomic fact up to a coarser declared grain, summing the additive measures over the collapsed dimensions.

problem_solution.problem: Common summary queries scan the whole atomic fact, so a rollup fact at a coarser grain is precomputed while staying consistent with the base totals.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent aggregates a semi-additive or non-additive measure by summing it across the wrong dimension, producing totals that disagree with the base fact.
problem_solution.solution: An aggregate capability that groups the atomic fact to the coarser grain, sums only additive measures, and reconciles the rolled-up totals to the base.
known_pitfalls: aggregate totals disagreeing with the base
duplicate rows at the aggregate grain
success_signals: aggregate measure totals reconcile to the base fact
one row per aggregate grain combination

blackbox.does: Builds an audit dimension capturing load lineage and data-quality context for each batch so fact rows can reference the conditions under which they were loaded.

problem_solution.problem: Analysts need to trace which load process, version, and quality condition produced a given fact row, which requires an audit dimension attached to the fact.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent scatters run metadata into free-text fact columns that cannot be filtered or joined for lineage questions.
problem_solution.solution: An audit-dimension capability that records one row per load context with a surrogate key the fact carries for lineage.
known_pitfalls: metadata stored inline on the fact
fact not carrying the audit key
success_signals: each fact row references a resolvable audit key
one audit row per distinct load context

blackbox.does: Builds a bridge table resolving a many-to-many relationship between a fact and a dimension by emitting one row per member of each group association.

problem_solution.problem: When a fact relates to many dimension members at once, such as an account with several owners, a direct foreign key cannot express the many-to-many association.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent pivots the members into repeated columns or duplicates the fact per member, corrupting the grain and double counting measures.
problem_solution.solution: A bridge capability that materializes a group key and one association row per member so the fact joins through the bridge at its true grain.
known_pitfalls: double counting measures through the bridge
success_signals: every association resolves to a real member
one row per group-member pair

blackbox.does: Builds a conformed dimension shared across business processes by standardizing keys, labels, and attribute domains to the enterprise bus-matrix definition.

problem_solution.problem: The same dimension used by several facts must present identical keys and labels everywhere so measures from different processes can be compared side by side.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent builds a separate lookalike dimension per mart with divergent labels, making cross-process drill-across joins meaningless.
problem_solution.solution: A conformance capability that maps each source to the shared attribute domain and publishes one dimension every mart references.
known_pitfalls: attribute domains not aligned to the standard
success_signals: all marts join on the same conformed key
labels match the bus-matrix definition

blackbox.does: Builds a consolidated fact that combines measures from multiple business processes at a common conformed grain so related metrics sit side by side on one row.

problem_solution.problem: Comparing measures from separate processes, such as sales actuals against forecast, is easier when they are consolidated to a shared grain on one fact rather than joined at query time.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent consolidates facts recorded at different grains without aligning them, so measures from one process are duplicated against the other.
problem_solution.solution: A consolidation capability that reduces each contributing fact to the common conformed grain and combines their measures on aligned dimension keys.
success_signals: each process measure reconciles to its source fact
one row per common grain combination

blackbox.does: Publishes a current-only view over a type-2 dimension by selecting the version flagged current per natural key so simple joins can ignore historical versions.

problem_solution.problem: Many queries only need the latest attributes of a member, so joining against a full type-2 history forces every consumer to filter for the current flag.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins facts to the full type-2 table without the current filter, fanning out every current row across all historical versions.
problem_solution.solution: A current-view capability that filters to the current version per natural key and exposes it as a simple one-row-per-member dimension.
known_pitfalls: more than one current row per key
view drifting from the source on refresh
consumers still joining the full history
success_signals: view has exactly one row per natural key
every row is flagged current

blackbox.does: Generates a calendar date dimension over a declared date range with one row per day carrying calendar and fiscal attributes and a stable date surrogate key.

problem_solution.problem: Almost every fact references a date, and a rich date dimension with calendar and fiscal attributes is needed so time analysis does not rely on raw date functions.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves gaps in the date range or derives fiscal periods inconsistently, so time series break and fiscal rollups disagree.
problem_solution.solution: A generator that emits one deterministic row per day across the range with calendar and fiscal attributes and a stable date key.
known_pitfalls: gaps or duplicate days in the range
time zone drift shifting day boundaries
success_signals: one row per day with no gaps
regenerating the same range yields identical rows

blackbox.does: Retains an operational transaction identifier such as an order or invoice number as a degenerate dimension column on the fact with no separate dimension table.

problem_solution.problem: A transaction number has no descriptive attributes of its own but is needed on the fact for grouping and drill-back, so it belongs on the fact as a degenerate dimension.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent builds a pointless one-column dimension table for the transaction number and joins to it, adding a needless key and join.
problem_solution.solution: A degenerate-dimension capability that carries the operational identifier directly on the fact and validates it at the declared grain.
known_pitfalls: identifier not unique at the fact grain
success_signals: the operational id is present on every fact row
the id is unique at the declared grain

blackbox.does: Builds a query-ready dimension table from cleaned staging rows, attaching the surrogate key and the descriptive attributes declared by the schema spec.

problem_solution.problem: A dimension must expose clean, deduplicated descriptive attributes keyed by a unique surrogate so downstream facts can join to exactly one row per member.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent copies staging rows straight through, leaving duplicate natural keys and null descriptive attributes that break fact joins.
problem_solution.solution: A build capability that deduplicates to one row per natural key, attaches the surrogate, and enforces the declared attribute schema before publishing.
known_pitfalls: duplicate natural keys reaching the dimension
surrogate not populated for the unknown member
attribute types drifting from the schema
success_signals: one row per natural key
surrogate key is unique and non-null

blackbox.does: Detects new, changed, and unchanged dimension members by hashing the tracked attribute set per natural key and emits a classified change set for a downstream merge.

problem_solution.problem: A slowly-changing-dimension merge needs to know which members are new versus changed versus unchanged, computed consistently from the tracked attributes.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent compares columns ad hoc and misses a tracked attribute, so real changes are classified as unchanged and history is lost.
problem_solution.solution: A change-detection capability that computes a stable hash over the declared tracked attributes and labels each row insert, update, or unchanged.
known_pitfalls: tracked attribute omitted from the hash
hash sensitive to column order or whitespace
success_signals: identical inputs yield an all-unchanged classification
each natural key appears once in the change set

blackbox.does: Verifies that a dimension conforms to the enterprise bus-matrix standard by checking that its keys, labels, and attribute domains match the shared definition across marts.

problem_solution.problem: Conformed dimensions only enable drill-across if every consuming mart truly shares the same keys and labels, which must be verified rather than assumed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent trusts that a dimension is conformed and lets a divergent copy through, quietly breaking cross-mart comparisons.
problem_solution.solution: A read-only check comparing the dimension's keys, labels, and domains against the bus-matrix standard and reporting any deviations.
known_pitfalls: attribute domains drifting from the standard
success_signals: zero conformance deviations reported
keys and labels match the bus-matrix standard

blackbox.does: Re-points fact rows that were keyed to inferred placeholder members onto the real surrogate keys once the true dimension members have been loaded.

problem_solution.problem: Facts keyed to placeholder members during early arrival must be corrected to the real surrogate keys after the dimension catches up, without disturbing already-correct rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent rewrites every fact key unconditionally, corrupting rows that were already pointing at the correct member.
problem_solution.solution: A backfill capability that finds facts still on placeholder keys, maps each to the resolved surrogate, and updates only those rows.
success_signals: no fact row remains on a placeholder key
re-running changes no additional rows

blackbox.does: Collapses duplicate natural-key candidates into one golden dimension row by applying survivorship rules that pick the surviving value for each attribute.

problem_solution.problem: Multiple source records can describe the same dimension member, and the dimension must present exactly one surviving value per attribute chosen by explicit rules.
