problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent keeps whichever duplicate loads last, so the surviving attribute values change nondeterministically between runs.
problem_solution.solution: A survivorship capability that groups by natural key and applies per-attribute precedence rules to produce one deterministic golden row.
known_pitfalls: survivorship rules not defined per attribute
duplicate golden rows for one key
success_signals: one golden row per natural key
re-running produces identical surviving values

blackbox.does: Performs a drill-across by separately aggregating two facts to their conformed dimensions and merging the two result sets on the conformed keys into one comparison mart.

problem_solution.problem: Comparing measures from two facts across shared dimensions must aggregate each fact separately before merging, or the join between two facts fans out the rows.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins the two facts directly on the shared keys, producing a many-to-many fan-out that multiplies both sets of measures.
problem_solution.solution: A drill-across capability that aggregates each fact to the conformed grain first, then full-joins the two summaries on the conformed keys.
known_pitfalls: joining raw facts and fanning out
missing keys dropping one side of the comparison
success_signals: each fact aggregates independently before the merge
measures reconcile to their source fact totals

blackbox.does: Verifies that every foreign key on a fact resolves to exactly one dimension surrogate key and reports any orphaned or unresolved fact rows.

problem_solution.problem: A star is only trustworthy if every fact foreign key points at a real dimension member, so orphaned keys must be detected before the mart is published.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent assumes integrity holds and publishes, so downstream inner joins silently drop orphaned fact rows and totals go wrong.
problem_solution.solution: A read-only check that anti-joins each fact foreign key against its dimension and reports the count and sample of unresolved keys.
known_pitfalls: null keys not counted as orphans
success_signals: zero orphaned foreign keys reported
every fact key resolves to one dimension member

blackbox.does: Applies the declared null policy to a fact by substituting the unknown-member key for null foreign keys and distinguishing genuine zero measures from missing ones.

problem_solution.problem: Null foreign keys break dimension joins and null measures are ambiguous, so facts need an explicit policy for unknown members and for zero versus missing values.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves null foreign keys in place, so inner joins silently drop those fact rows and totals understate.
problem_solution.solution: A null-handling capability that maps null keys to the unknown member and applies the declared zero-versus-null rule to measures.
known_pitfalls: null keys dropping rows on inner joins
unknown member not defined in the dimension
success_signals: no fact foreign key is null
row count is preserved through handling

blackbox.does: Builds a factless fact capturing the occurrence or coverage of an event as dimension key combinations with no numeric measures, supporting counting and coverage analysis.

problem_solution.problem: Some questions are about whether an event happened or what was eligible but did not happen, which is captured by a fact of key combinations with no measures.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent invents a dummy measure column of ones and treats it as additive, confusing counting semantics and inviting misuse.
problem_solution.solution: A factless-fact capability that records the dimension key combination at the declared grain so events are counted by row and coverage gaps are found by anti-join.
known_pitfalls: duplicate key combinations at the grain
success_signals: one row per key combination at the grain
counts derive from row counts not a measure

blackbox.does: Declares the intended grain of a fact as a column set and enforces it by verifying that the declared grain columns are unique across the table.

problem_solution.problem: Every fact and dimension has exactly one intended grain, and a table silently carrying duplicates at that grain corrupts every measure aggregated from it.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent never states the grain, so a subtle join duplicates rows and the error is only noticed as inflated totals much later.
problem_solution.solution: A capability that records the declared grain columns and asserts they form a unique key, reporting any duplicate grain combinations.
known_pitfalls: duplicates at the grain going unnoticed
success_signals: the declared grain columns are unique
no duplicate grain combinations reported

blackbox.does: Builds a hierarchy bridge, a closure table enumerating every ancestor-descendant pair with depth for a ragged variable-depth parent-child dimension.

problem_solution.problem: A ragged variable-depth hierarchy such as an org chart cannot be queried by fixed level columns, so rollups need every ancestor-descendant relationship enumerated.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent hard-codes a fixed number of level columns and truncates or nulls branches deeper or shallower than that fixed depth.
problem_solution.solution: A closure-bridge capability that emits one row for every ancestor-descendant pair with the distance between them, including self pairs at depth zero.
known_pitfalls: self pairs at depth zero omitted
success_signals: walking the bridge reconstructs the original edges
every node has a self pair at depth zero

blackbox.does: Flattens a fixed-depth balanced hierarchy into named level columns on the dimension so each level can be selected and grouped without recursive traversal.

problem_solution.problem: A balanced fixed-depth hierarchy such as category to subcategory to product is easiest to slice when each level is its own column on the dimension.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent flattens with the levels in the wrong order or drops a level, so rollups group by the wrong parent.
problem_solution.solution: A flatten capability that maps each hierarchy level to a named column in the declared order and preserves the parent-child linkage.
known_pitfalls: level columns in the wrong order
success_signals: reassembling the levels reproduces the source hierarchy
one row per leaf member

blackbox.does: Creates inferred placeholder dimension rows for natural keys that arrive on facts before the dimension load so referential integrity holds until the real attributes arrive.

problem_solution.problem: An early-arriving fact can reference a dimension member the dimension load has not yet seen, which would otherwise break the fact-to-dimension foreign key.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent drops the fact row or points it at a shared unknown member, losing the ability to backfill the real member later.
problem_solution.solution: An inferred-member capability that inserts a placeholder dimension row with the natural key and an inferred flag so the fact can be keyed and later corrected.
known_pitfalls: placeholders never reconciled to real members
inferred flag not cleared on backfill
success_signals: every early fact key resolves to a placeholder
re-running creates no duplicate placeholders

blackbox.does: Collapses several low-cardinality flags and indicators into a single junk dimension holding one row per distinct combination of the flag values.

problem_solution.problem: Scattering many yes/no flags and small codes directly on the fact bloats it, so the low-cardinality attributes are grouped into one junk dimension.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent enumerates every possible flag combination up front, creating a huge sparse dimension most of whose rows are never referenced.
problem_solution.solution: A junk-dimension capability that materializes only the flag combinations that actually occur and assigns each a surrogate key.
success_signals: one row per observed flag combination
re-running adds only genuinely new combinations

blackbox.does: Inserts a back-dated type-2 version for a dimension change that arrives after the fact events it should apply to and adjusts surrounding validity intervals to keep the timeline consistent.

problem_solution.problem: A dimension change can be reported with an effective date in the past, requiring a new version inserted into the middle of an existing type-2 history rather than appended at the end.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent appends the change as a current version, leaving prior facts joined to the wrong version and the timeline overlapping.
problem_solution.solution: A late-arrival capability that places the back-dated version at its effective date, splits the affected interval, and repairs adjacent validity bounds.
success_signals: validity intervals remain contiguous and non-overlapping
re-applying the same late change makes no further edits

blackbox.does: Tags each fact measure as additive, semi-additive, or non-additive and records the dimensions across which each measure may be safely summed as a data contract.

problem_solution.problem: Not every measure can be summed across every dimension, so each measure needs an explicit additivity classification to prevent invalid aggregations downstream.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent sums a semi-additive balance across time or a ratio across anything, producing figures that look plausible but are wrong.
problem_solution.solution: A tagging capability that classifies each measure and records the allowed and disallowed aggregation dimensions in a machine-readable contract.
known_pitfalls: summing a semi-additive balance over time
success_signals: every measure carries an additivity tag
disallowed aggregations are recorded in the contract

blackbox.does: Splits the rapidly changing attributes out of a large dimension into a separate mini-dimension of banded profiles that the fact references directly.

problem_solution.problem: When a few attributes of a large dimension change frequently, keeping them inline forces constant type-2 versioning of the whole big dimension.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent leaves the volatile attributes inline and type-2 versions the entire dimension, multiplying rows and slowing joins.
problem_solution.solution: A mini-dimension capability that moves the volatile attributes into a compact banded profile dimension whose key is carried on the fact.
known_pitfalls: fact not carrying the mini-dimension key
success_signals: base dimension versions far less often
each fact row carries a valid mini-dimension key

blackbox.does: Assigns allocation weighting factors to the rows of a multivalued bridge so that measures apportioned across group members sum back to the original fact total.

problem_solution.problem: Joining a fact through a multivalued bridge multiplies its measures across every member, so a weighting factor is needed to apportion the measure without inflating totals.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins through the bridge with no weighting factor, so a shared measure is counted once per member and the totals balloon.
problem_solution.solution: A weighting capability that computes an allocation factor per association so weighted measures reconcile to the unallocated fact total.
known_pitfalls: weights within a group not summing to one
success_signals: allocation factors sum to one per group
weighted measure totals reconcile to the fact

blackbox.does: Denormalizes a star by joining the fact to its dimensions into one wide table that carries the measures alongside the descriptive attributes on every row.

problem_solution.problem: Some query engines and BI tools perform best against a single wide table, so a star is flattened into one denormalized table with measures and attributes together.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins to a non-unique dimension and fans out the fact rows, silently inflating the flattened row count and the measures.
problem_solution.solution: A flatten capability that joins the fact to each dimension on a verified unique key and confirms the wide row count equals the fact row count.
success_signals: wide row count equals the fact row count
no measure is duplicated by flattening

blackbox.does: Attaches an outrigger dimension referenced from within a primary dimension, such as a date dimension linked from a customer dimension, via a controlled foreign key.

problem_solution.problem: A dimension sometimes needs to reference another well-defined dimension, such as a first-purchase date, without repeating all of that dimension's attributes inline.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inlines the entire referenced dimension into the primary one, duplicating attributes and coupling their refresh cycles.
problem_solution.solution: An outrigger capability that stores a single foreign key from the primary dimension to the referenced dimension and validates the reference.
success_signals: every outrigger key resolves to one member
primary dimension avoids duplicating outrigger attributes

blackbox.does: Builds a periodic-snapshot fact with one row per entity per regular period, capturing the measured state at the close of each period.

problem_solution.problem: Some processes are best measured at regular intervals, such as a daily account balance, requiring one fact row per entity per period even when nothing changed.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent only writes rows for periods with activity, leaving gaps that make period-over-period trends and dense time series impossible.
problem_solution.solution: A periodic-snapshot capability that emits a row for every entity in every period at the declared grain, carrying the end-of-period measures.
known_pitfalls: measures captured mid-period instead of at close
success_signals: one row per entity per period with no gaps
row count equals entities times periods

blackbox.does: Resolves each fact row to the type-2 dimension version whose validity interval contains the fact event timestamp, performing an as-of join on natural key and time.

problem_solution.problem: A fact must join to the dimension version that was in effect when the event occurred, not the current version, which requires matching on the validity interval.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins on natural key alone and matches every historical version, fanning out the fact rows or picking the wrong version.
problem_solution.solution: An as-of capability that selects the single version whose effective and expiry bounds bracket the event timestamp for each natural key.
known_pitfalls: row fan-out from matching multiple versions
events outside any interval left unmatched
success_signals: input and output fact counts reconcile
each fact matches exactly one dimension version

blackbox.does: Exposes one physical dimension under multiple named roles by publishing role-specific views with aliased keys and attribute prefixes for each foreign key on the fact.

problem_solution.problem: A fact may reference one dimension several times in distinct roles, such as a date dimension used as order date, ship date, and due date, and each role needs unambiguous column names.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent copies the dimension once per role, so the same member drifts between copies and storage is wasted.
problem_solution.solution: A role-playing capability that keeps one physical dimension and generates aliased role views so each fact foreign key joins to a clearly named role.
known_pitfalls: physically duplicating the dimension per role
roles drifting out of sync with the base
success_signals: every role resolves to the same physical member
each role view has unambiguous key and attribute names

blackbox.does: Applies type-0 handling to durable dimension attributes by preserving the original loaded value and ignoring later source changes on the type-0 columns.

problem_solution.problem: Some dimension attributes such as original credit score or first-seen date must retain their initially loaded value permanently even when the source later reports a different value.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites the attribute with whatever the source last sent, destroying the durable original value the reports depend on.
problem_solution.solution: A type-0 capability that inserts the value on first arrival and thereafter ignores incoming changes to the designated retain columns.
known_pitfalls: a later load overwriting the original value
retain columns not covered by the policy
success_signals: type-0 values never change after first load
re-running a batch changes no retain columns

blackbox.does: Applies type-1 handling by overwriting changed descriptive attributes in place on the current dimension row, keeping no prior history of the changed values.

problem_solution.problem: For attributes where only the latest value matters, a changed source value must overwrite the current dimension row without spawning new versions.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inserts a new row on every change, silently converting a type-1 attribute into an accidental type-2 history and multiplying rows per key.
problem_solution.solution: A type-1 capability that matches on the natural key, updates the changed attributes in place, and leaves exactly one row per key.
known_pitfalls: overwrite losing a value needed for audit
duplicate keys created by a bad match
success_signals: exactly one row per natural key after merge
re-applying the same batch updates zero rows

blackbox.does: Applies type-2 handling by closing the current version of a changed key with an expiry date and opening a new current version carrying effective and expiry validity bounds and a current flag.

problem_solution.problem: Dimensions that must preserve history need each attribute change to close the prior version and open a new one so facts join to the version that was current at the event time.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent updates the row in place or leaves several rows flagged current, destroying history or breaking as-of joins from the facts.
problem_solution.solution: A type-2 capability that detects tracked-attribute changes, stamps an expiry on the prior current row, and inserts a new current row with validity bounds.
known_pitfalls: overlapping validity intervals for one key
multiple rows flagged current for one key
success_signals: exactly one current row per natural key
re-running the same batch opens no new versions

blackbox.does: Applies type-3 handling by shifting the current attribute value into a prior-value column and writing the new value into the current column, retaining a single alternate history step.

problem_solution.problem: Some analyses need to compare the current attribute value against its immediately preceding value without maintaining full row history.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent overwrites the current value and never populates the prior-value column, leaving the alternate-history comparison impossible.
problem_solution.solution: A type-3 capability that copies the outgoing current value into the prior column and records the effective date of the change before writing the new value.
known_pitfalls: a second change silently discarding the prior value
prior column not initialized on first load
success_signals: prior column holds the last superseded value
one row per natural key retained

blackbox.does: Applies type-4 handling by keeping a compact current dimension and pushing each superseded version into a separate history table keyed by the same natural key.

problem_solution.problem: A rapidly changing dimension can bloat if all versions live in one table, so the current row is kept lean while superseded versions move to a history sidecar.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent updates the current table but forgets to archive the outgoing version, so history is lost and the sidecar drifts out of sync.
problem_solution.solution: A type-4 capability that writes the outgoing version to the history table before overwriting the current row, keeping both keyed consistently.
known_pitfalls: outgoing version not archived before overwrite
history and current tables using different keys
success_signals: current table holds one row per key
every superseded version appears once in history

blackbox.does: Applies type-6 hybrid handling by opening type-2 versioned rows while also overwriting a current-value column on every version so both historical and current attributes are available on one row.

problem_solution.problem: Some reports need both the attribute value as of the event (type-2) and the member's latest value (type-1) available together on every historical row.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent maintains only versioned rows and forgets to propagate the current value back across prior versions, so current-value reporting is wrong.
problem_solution.solution: A type-6 capability that opens a new type-2 version on change and updates the current-value column on all versions of the key.
known_pitfalls: current-value column not propagated to old versions
success_signals: every version of a key shares the same current value
exactly one row per key is flagged current

blackbox.does: Normalizes a denormalized dimension into a snowflake set of related sub-dimension tables linked by foreign keys so shared attribute levels are stored once.

problem_solution.problem: A wide denormalized dimension can repeat higher-level attributes across many rows, and normalizing them into linked sub-dimensions removes that repetition.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent splits out a sub-dimension but drops or mismatches the foreign keys, so rejoining no longer reproduces the original rows.
problem_solution.solution: A normalize capability that factors repeating attribute levels into sub-dimensions with foreign keys such that rejoining reconstructs the source dimension exactly.
known_pitfalls: foreign keys not reproducing the join
attribute values lost during the split
success_signals: rejoining the snowflake reproduces the source dimension
each sub-dimension key is unique

blackbox.does: Assembles a query-ready star-schema mart by binding a central fact to its conformed dimensions under a declared join policy while preserving the fact grain.

problem_solution.problem: Consumers need a fact wired to its dimensions as a coherent star so business questions can be answered by simple joins without knowing the load internals.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent joins the fact to a dimension on a non-unique key, fanning out the fact rows and multiplying the measures.
problem_solution.solution: An assembly capability that verifies each dimension key is unique, binds the fact to its dimensions, and confirms the fact grain survives the joins.
known_pitfalls: measures multiplied by a bad join
success_signals: assembled row count matches the fact row count
every fact key resolves to one dimension row

blackbox.does: Builds a supertype dimension of attributes common to all entity types plus subtype dimensions of the type-specific attributes for heterogeneous members.

problem_solution.problem: A dimension covering heterogeneous entities such as varied product lines has some shared attributes and many type-specific ones that would be sparse if flattened together.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent flattens every type-specific attribute into one wide dimension, producing a mostly-null sparse table hard to query per type.
problem_solution.solution: A supertype/subtype capability that publishes the common attributes once and factors the type-specific attributes into subtype tables sharing the key.
known_pitfalls: subtype keys not aligned to the supertype
success_signals: supertype holds one row per member
each subtype row resolves to its supertype key

blackbox.does: Assigns a stable warehouse-managed surrogate key to each distinct natural key in a staging table and returns the natural-to-surrogate key map plus a run receipt.

problem_solution.problem: Facts and dimensions must join on compact warehouse-owned keys rather than volatile source natural keys, and each natural key must always resolve to the same surrogate across runs.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent mints a new sequence value on every load, so the same natural key gets multiple surrogates and prior fact rows point at abandoned keys.
problem_solution.solution: A key-assignment capability that looks up an existing surrogate for a natural key and only allocates a new one for a genuinely new key, recording the mapping.
known_pitfalls: collisions when the natural key is not unique
hash keys colliding on truncated inputs
success_signals: re-running a load allocates zero new keys
each natural key maps to exactly one surrogate

blackbox.does: Resolves the natural keys on incoming fact staging rows to dimension surrogate keys using a supplied key map and returns the keyed staging table.

problem_solution.problem: During fact loading each natural key must be swapped for its dimension surrogate key, and rows whose key is missing from the dimension must be routed rather than silently dropped.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent inner-joins facts to dimensions and loses every row whose natural key is not yet in the dimension, understating the measures.
problem_solution.solution: A lookup capability that left-joins the key map, counts resolved versus unresolved rows, and directs unresolved rows to an inferred-key path.
known_pitfalls: duplicate surrogates from a non-unique key map
unknown member not substituted for nulls
success_signals: input and output row counts reconcile
every emitted fact row carries a valid surrogate

blackbox.does: Generates a time-of-day dimension with one row per second or minute of the day carrying hour, minute, and named buckets such as shift and daypart with a stable key.

problem_solution.problem: Analyzing events by time of day is awkward against raw timestamps, so a separate time-of-day dimension provides hour, minute, and named period buckets.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent folds time of day into the date dimension, multiplying its rows by every second and bloating a table that should stay small.
problem_solution.solution: A generator that emits one deterministic row per unit of the day at the declared granularity with named buckets, kept separate from the date dimension.
known_pitfalls: combining time of day into the date dimension
bucket boundaries overlapping or leaving gaps
duplicate time units in the range
success_signals: one row per time unit at the declared granularity
regenerating yields identical rows and buckets

blackbox.does: Builds a transaction-grain fact with one row per business event, carrying the dimension surrogate keys and the additive measures captured at that event.

problem_solution.problem: The most atomic fact records one row per discrete business event with foreign keys to every relevant dimension and the measures observed at that moment.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent pre-aggregates the events during the build, destroying the atomic grain and the ability to drill to individual transactions.
problem_solution.solution: A transaction-fact capability that keeps one row per event, resolves all dimension keys, and validates the declared event grain.
known_pitfalls: premature aggregation losing the atomic grain
success_signals: one row per business event at the declared grain
every dimension key resolves

blackbox.does: Normalizes a wide one-big-table back into a star by extracting the dimension attribute groups into keyed dimensions and reducing the remainder to a keyed fact at the declared grain.

problem_solution.problem: A wide table that repeats descriptive attributes on every row is expensive to maintain, and normalizing it into a fact plus dimensions removes the repetition while staying reconstructable.
problem_solution.naive_agent_failure: An agent extracts a dimension but assigns keys inconsistently, so re-flattening the star no longer reproduces the original wide table.
problem_solution.solution: A normalize capability that groups the attributes into dimensions with stable keys and reduces the measures to a fact such that re-joining reproduces the wide rows.
known_pitfalls: inconsistent keys breaking the round trip
grain not preserved on the fact
success_signals: re-flattening the star reproduces the wide table
each extracted dimension key is unique
